children.text: mānuṣyaṃ samavāpya duṣkaraśatair labdhvā durāpaṃ kṣaṇaṃ
children.translated_text: Having obtained human birth through hundreds of difficult [deeds], having gained this hard-to-attain moment,

children.text: mṛtyau niṣpratikāradāruṇatare nityaṃ puraḥsthāyini /
children.translated_text: while death, most terrible and irresistible, ever stands before [them],

children.text: pātheyaṃ damadānasaṃyamamayaṃ yair na prabhūtaṃ kṛtaṃ
children.translated_text: those who have not abundantly prepared the provisions of self-control, charity, and restraint

children.text: saṃsārogramaruprapātapatitāḥ prāpsyanti duḥkhāni te // SRKK_1 //
children.translated_text: will fall into the precipice of the dreadful illness of <s>saṃsāra</s> and experience [only] suffering. // SRKK 1 //

body.translated_text: I. The Story Encouraging Merit (<s>Puṇya</s>)

children.text: mānuṣyaṃ durlabhaṃ prāpya vidyutsaṃpātacañcalam /
children.translated_text: Having obtained the rare human birth, flickering like a flash of lightning,

children.text: bhavakṣaye matiḥ kāryā bhavopakaraṇeṣu vā // SRKK_2 //
children.translated_text: one should set one's mind on the cessation of existence, or [at least] on the means of [improving] existence. // SRKK 2 //

children.text: manuṣyatvaṃ samāsādya vidyujjvālormicañcalam /
children.translated_text: Having attained human life, flickering like a lightning-flash upon a wave,

children.text: puṇyam evātra kurvīta yataś cintāmaṇir nṛṇām // SRKK_3 //
children.translated_text: one should practice merit (<s>puṇya</s>) alone here, for it is the wish-fulfilling jewel (<s>cintāmaṇi</s>) for humans. // SRKK 3 //

children.text: yasyānubhāvān mānuṣyaṃ prāptaṃ bhūyo 'pi sāṃpratam /
children.translated_text: By whose power you have now again obtained human birth —

children.text: puṇyaṃ tad vardhyasveha yasmād dhetuḥ sukhasya te // SRKK_4 //
children.translated_text: increase that merit, for it is the cause of your happiness. // SRKK 4 //

children.text: mānuṣyaṃ yadupāśrayeṇa bhavatā labdhaṃ punaḥ sāṃprataṃ
children.translated_text: This human birth that you have now obtained again through its support,

children.text: rūpaudāryakulonnatiprabhṛtibhir yuktaṃ vicitrair guṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: endowed with marvelous qualities such as beauty, generosity, noble lineage, and the like —

children.text: tat puṇyaṃ suhṛd eka eva jagatāṃ bandhuś ca janmāntare
children.translated_text: that merit is the sole friend and kinsman of beings in the next life;

children.text: tasmāt tūrṇam idaṃ kuru tvam asakṛt sarvārthasaṃpatkaram // SRKK_5 //
children.translated_text: therefore, quickly perform it again and again — it is the fulfillment of all aims. // SRKK 5 //

children.text: lakṣmīniketaṃ yadupāśrayeṇa prāpto 'si lokābhimataṃ prabhutvam /
children.translated_text: By whose support you have attained lordship, the abode of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, desired by the world —

children.text: tāny eva puṇyāni vivardhayethā na karṣaṇīyo hy upakāripakṣaḥ // SRKK_6 //
children.translated_text: you should increase those very merits; for the party of benefactors should not be diminished. // SRKK 6 //

children.text: viramata pāpataḥ kuruta puṇyam udārataraṃ
children.translated_text: Desist from sin! Perform merit most generously!

children.text: damayata durdamaṃ viṣayalolamanasturagam /
children.translated_text: Tame the difficult-to-tame horse of the mind, restless toward sense-objects!

children.text: bhavata munīndravat parahitābhiratāḥ satataṃ
children.translated_text: Be always devoted to the welfare of others, like the chief of sages,

children.text: daśati na yāvad eva maraṇāhir asahyaviṣaḥ // SRKK_7 //
children.translated_text: before the serpent of death with its unbearable poison bites! // SRKK 7 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the Story Encouraging Merit //

children.text: jalanidhikūrmakanṭhayugarandhrasamāgamavat
children.translated_text: Like the meeting of a turtle's neck with the hole in a yoke [floating] on the ocean,

children.text: kṣaṇam anavāpyam adbhutam imaṃ samavetya calam /
children.translated_text: having encountered this amazing, fleeting, unattainable moment,

children.text: praśamapuraikavartma vinipātabhayāpaharaṃ
children.translated_text: the sole path to the city of peace, which removes the fear of falling [into lower births] —

children.text: śṛṇuta sudurlabhaṃ kṣaṇam apīha muner vacanam // SRKK_8 //
children.translated_text: listen, even for a moment, to the word of the Sage, so difficult to obtain! // SRKK 8 //

body.translated_text: II. The Story Encouraging the Hearing of <s>Dharma</s>

children.text: yad durlabham kalpaśatair anekair mānuṣyam aṣṭākṣaṇadoṣamuktam /
children.translated_text: This human birth, free from the eight unfavorable conditions, difficult to obtain in countless aeons —

children.text: tat sāṃprataṃ prāptam ato bhavadbhiḥ kāryo hi dharmaśravaṇāya yatnaḥ // SRKK_9 //
children.translated_text: having now obtained it, effort should be made by you for the hearing of <s>Dharma</s>. // SRKK 9 //

children.text: pallavāgrajalabinducañcale kleśajālapariveṣṭite bhave /
children.translated_text: In this existence, flickering like a water-drop on the tip of a leaf, enveloped by a net of afflictions,

children.text: yo na cintayati karmasatpatham tasya janma bhavatīha niṣphalam // SRKK_10 //
children.translated_text: he who does not contemplate the good path of <s>karma</s> — his birth is fruitless here. // SRKK 10 //

children.text: na narakagataiḥ pretais tiryaggatair vikalendriyair
children.translated_text: Neither by those gone to hell, nor by <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), nor by animals, nor by those with impaired senses,

children.text: amaragurubhiḥ pratyantasthaiḥ kudṛkkaravikṣataiḥ /
children.translated_text: nor by the long-lived gods, nor by those dwelling in border-regions, nor by those afflicted by wrong views,

children.text: munisavitari prajñālokena cānudite jine
children.translated_text: nor [born] before the sun-like Sage, the <s>Jina</s>, has risen with the light of wisdom,

children.text: sanaravibudhaiḥ śakyaṃ pātuṃ munīndravacomṛtam // SRKK_11 //
children.translated_text: can the nectar of the words of the chief of sages be drunk — even by gods and wise men [under those conditions]. // SRKK 11 //

children.text: tasmāt kukāryam vyapahāya sarvaṃ matvā svakāryaṃ paramāryadharmam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, abandoning all evil deeds, regarding the supreme noble <s>Dharma</s> as one's own duty,

children.text: śrotavya eva prayatena dharmo yasmād ataḥ sarvaguṇā bhavanti // SRKK_12 //
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> should indeed be heard with effort, for from it arise all virtues. // SRKK 12 //

children.text: maunīndraṃ vākyaratnam janayati sudhiyām etad ādau pramodaṃ
children.translated_text: This jewel-word of the lord of silent sages first produces delight in the wise

children.text: śrotrāpāte tataś ca prabalagurughanadhvāntavṛndaṃ nihanti /
children.translated_text: upon reaching the ears; then it destroys the dense mass of thick darkness [of ignorance];

children.text: cintādhyānāvasāne sphuṭayati sakalam janmacakraprabandhaṃ
children.translated_text: at the conclusion of contemplation and meditation, it shatters the entire cycle of births,

children.text: niḥśeṣātaṅkapaṅktiṃ vighaṭayati sadā sarvasaṃpannidhānam // SRKK_13 //
children.translated_text: always disperses every train of afflictions, and is a treasury of all blessings. // SRKK 13 //

children.text: harati tīvrabhavaprabhavāpadaṃ diśati nirvṛtisaukhyam anuttaram /
children.translated_text: It removes the calamity born from the fierce [cycle of] existence and bestows the unsurpassed happiness of <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation).

children.text: tad idam evam avetya muner vacaḥ śṛṇuta saṃprati nirmalamānasāḥ // SRKK_14 //
children.translated_text: Knowing the Sage's word to be thus, listen now with purified minds. // SRKK 14 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the Story Encouraging the Hearing of <s>Dharma</s> //

children.text: III. Durlabhamanuṣyakatha
children.translated_text: III. The Story of the Rarity of Human Birth

children.text: yat prāpya janmajaladher api yānti pāram āropayanti śivam uttamabodhibījam /
children.translated_text: Having attained it, [beings] cross even the ocean of birth; they plant the supreme seed of awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) auspiciously.

children.text: cintāmaṇer api samabhyadhikaṃ guṇaughair mānuṣyakaṃ ka iha tad viphalī karoti // SRKK_15 //
children.translated_text: Surpassing even the wish-fulfilling jewel in its flood of virtues — who would render this human birth fruitless? // SRKK 15 //

children.text: yo manuṣyaṃ kuśalavibhavaiḥ prāpya kalpair analpair
children.translated_text: He who, having obtained human birth through countless aeons of meritorious wealth,

children.text: mohāt puṇyadraviṇam iha na svalpam apy ācinoti /
children.translated_text: through delusion does not accumulate even a small amount of the riches of merit here —

children.text: so 'smāl lokāt param upagatas tīvram abhyeti śokaṃ
children.translated_text: he, having departed from this world to the next, experiences intense grief,

children.text: ratnadvīpād vaṇig iva gataḥ svaṃ gṛhaṃ śūnyahastaḥ // SRKK_16 //
children.translated_text: like a merchant who returns home from an island of jewels with empty hands. // SRKK 16 //

children.text: nākuśalaiḥ karmapathair mānuṣyaṃ labhyate punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Human birth is not obtained again through unwholesome paths of <s>karma</s>.

children.text: alabhyamāne mānuṣye duḥkham eva kutaḥ sukham // SRKK_17 //
children.translated_text: When human birth is not obtained, there is only suffering — whence happiness? // SRKK 17 //

children.text: nātaḥ paraṃ vañcanāsti na ca moho 'sty ataḥ param /
children.translated_text: There is no greater self-deception than this, no greater delusion —

children.text: yad īdṛśaṃ kṣaṇaṃ prāpya na kuryāt kuśalaṃ bahu // SRKK_18 //
children.translated_text: that having obtained such a [precious] moment, one does not perform abundant good deeds. // SRKK 18 //

children.text: ekakṣaṇakṛtāt pāpād avīcau kalpam āsyate /
children.translated_text: For a sin committed in a single moment, one dwells in <s>Avīci</s> [hell] for an aeon.

children.text: naikajanmakṛtāt pāpāt kā punaḥ sugatau kathā // SRKK_19 //
children.translated_text: What then of [the consequences of] sin committed over many lifetimes — how much worse the result for the well-born! // SRKK 19 //

children.text: ata evāha bhagavān mānuṣyam atidurlabham /
children.translated_text: For this reason the Blessed One said that human birth is extremely rare —

children.text: mahārṇavayugacchidrakūrmagrīvārpanopamam // SRKK_20 //
children.translated_text: comparable to a turtle's neck passing through the hole in a yoke [floating] on the great ocean. // SRKK 20 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the Story of the Rarity of Human Birth //

children.text: IV. Dānakathā
children.translated_text: IV. The Story of Generosity (<s>Dāna</s>)

children.text: annapānaśayanāsanasaṃpad ratnamālyavasanābharaṇāni /
children.translated_text: Food, drink, beds, and seats, jewels, garlands, garments, and ornaments,

children.text: kīrtir uttamaguṇāś ca yuvatyo dānataḥ kathitam etad aśesam // SRKK_21 //
children.translated_text: fame, excellent virtues, and young women — all this has been declared [to come] from generosity. // SRKK 21 //

children.text: ājñādīptir bhogasaṃpat prakṛṣṭā rūpaudāryaṃ varṇamādhuryam ojaḥ /
children.translated_text: Radiant authority, excellent enjoyment of pleasures, beauty, generosity, charm of complexion, vigor,

children.text: vāksaubhāgyaṃ kāntir ārogyam āyus tat tad dānād iṣṭam iṣṭaṃ phalaṃ ca // SRKK_22 //
children.translated_text: eloquence of speech, grace, health, and long life — each desired fruit comes from the corresponding gift. // SRKK 22 //

children.text: aśvāḥ kṣaumāṇi nāgā bahukusumasitaṃ cāmaraṃ cātapatraṃ
children.translated_text: Horses, silk garments, elephants, a white fly-whisk adorned with many flowers, a royal parasol,

children.text: saudhaṃ saṃgītigarbhaṃ madhupaṭaharavāḥ puṣpamālā yuvatyaḥ /
children.translated_text: a palace filled with music, the sounds of drums and sweet instruments, garlands of flowers, young women,

children.text: bhojyaṃ ratnāni hārāḥ puranagaramahīṃ kuṅkumaṃ devalokaḥ
children.translated_text: food, jewels, necklaces, cities, kingdoms, lands, saffron, the world of the gods,

children.text: saṃbuddhatvaṃ ca buddhaiḥ kathitam iha phalaṃ dānakalpadrumasya // SRKK_23 //
children.translated_text: and perfect <s>Buddhahood</s> itself — the <s>Buddhas</s> have declared these as the fruits of the wish-granting tree of generosity. // SRKK 23 //

children.text: yan nīlotpalakomalāmaladalapraspardhinetrāḥ striyaś
children.translated_text: That women with eyes rivaling the soft, pure petals of blue lotuses,

children.text: cañcanmekhalacumbitorujaghanā visrastaraktāṃśukāḥ /
children.translated_text: with tinkling girdles kissing their thighs and hips, their red garments slipping away,

children.text: dāsyaṃ yānti vikampitastanataṭā vyāvalgitabhrūlatās
children.translated_text: come as servants, with trembling breasts and playfully arching brows —

children.text: tan mātsaryakapāṭapāṭanapaṭor dānasya visphūrjitam // SRKK_24 //
children.translated_text: that is the thunderbolt-power of generosity, which shatters the door-bolt of miserliness. // SRKK 24 //

children.text: aśvaiś cāmarabhāranāmitaśirorūpaiḥ khalīnonmukhair
children.translated_text: That noble men go forth on horses with heads bowed under the weight of fly-whisks, mouths lifted by reins,

children.text: nāgair bhinnamadaiś ca yan naravarā gacchanti chattrocchrayaiḥ /
children.translated_text: and on elephants streaming with rut,

children.text: bhṛtyaiḥ sābharaṇaiḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭair abhyarcyamānāḥ sadā
children.translated_text: always worshipped by ornamented servants with joined palms, beneath raised parasols —

children.text: tad dānasya phalaṃ vadanti munayaḥ pūrvārjitasyedṛśam // SRKK_25 //
children.translated_text: the sages declare this to be the fruit of generosity previously earned — such is it. // SRKK 25 //

children.text: hārair vajravicitrahemavalayair yat pārthivā bhūṣitāḥ
children.translated_text: That kings are adorned with necklaces, golden bracelets set with diamonds,

children.text: keyūrair mukuṭaiś ca ratnakhacitaiḥ siṃhāsanasthāḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: arm-bands, and jewel-studded crowns, always seated upon lion-thrones,

children.text: madhye 'ntaḥpurikājanasya vividhaiḥ krīḍanti vikrīḍitais
children.translated_text: sporting with various amusements amidst the women of the inner palace —

children.text: tad dānasya phalaṃ vadanti munayaḥ śārdūlavikrīḍitam // SRKK_26 //
children.translated_text: the sages declare this to be the fruit of generosity, in the <s>Śārdūlavikrīḍita</s> [meter]. // SRKK 26 //

children.text: prāsāde maṇiratnahemakhacite chattradhvajālaṃkṛte
children.translated_text: In a palace inlaid with gems, jewels, and gold, adorned with parasols and banners,

children.text: vīṇāvallariveṇugītamudite ratnaprabhodbhāsite /
children.translated_text: resounding with the music of <s>vīṇās</s>, flutes, and songs, brilliant with the radiance of jewels —

children.text: yac chakro ramate śacīsahacaro yoṣitsahasrākule
children.translated_text: that <s>Indra</s>, accompanied by <s>Śacī</s>, delights amidst thousands of women

children.text: tad dānasya phalaṃ vadanti munayaḥ pūrvārjitasyedṛśam // SRKK_27 //
children.translated_text: — the sages declare this to be the fruit of generosity previously earned — such is it. // SRKK 27 //

children.text: dātā priyatvam upayāti janasya śaśvat saṃsevyate ca baḥubhiḥ samupetya sadbhiḥ /
children.translated_text: A giver always becomes dear to people; he is attended by many good people who come to him.

children.text: kīrtiś ca dikṣu visaraty amalaṃ yaśo 'sya tat tat padaṃ samupayāti viśārado 'sau // SRKK_28 //
children.translated_text: His pure fame spreads in all directions — he attains each and every station, being accomplished. // SRKK 28 //

children.text: bhedāt kāyasya deveṣv avikalavividhottaptabhogāspadeṣu
children.translated_text: At the breaking of the body, being born among the gods — places of fully ripened, varied, and excellent enjoyments,

children.text: prāpyotpattiṃ vicitrastabakakusumitasphītakalpadrumeṣu /
children.translated_text: in gardens with lavish wish-granting trees blooming with clusters of diverse blossoms,

children.text: udyāneṣu prakāmaṃ suciram atisukhaṃ nandanādiṣv akhinnaḥ
children.translated_text: in <s>Nandana</s> and other [celestial] parks, unwearied, [enjoying] supremely great happiness for a long time,

children.text: prāpnoty utkṛṣṭarūpāmarayuvatijanaiḥ sevyamānaḥ pradānāt // SRKK_29 //
children.translated_text: one obtains [the company of] celestial women of supreme beauty — [all] through generosity. // SRKK 29 //

children.text: dānaṃ nāma mahānidhānam anugaṃ caurādyasādhāraṇaṃ
children.translated_text: Generosity is a great treasure that follows [one after death], not shared with thieves and others.

children.text: dānaṃ matsaralobhadoṣarajasaḥ prakṣālaṇaṃ cetasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Generosity is the washing away of the dust of envy, greed, and the faults [of the mind].

children.text: saṃsārādhvapariśramāpanayanaṃ dānaṃ sukhaṃ vāhanaṃ
children.translated_text: Generosity is the pleasant vehicle that removes the weariness of the road of <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: dānaṃ naikasukhopadhānasumukhaṃ sanmitram ātyantikam // SRKK_30 //
children.translated_text: Generosity is a good friend, ultimate and fair-faced, bestowing manifold comforts. // SRKK 30 //

children.text: śroṇīsaṃgatamekhalāḥ kalagiro līlācalaikabhruvaḥ
children.translated_text: With girdles fastened at their hips, with melodious voices, with one brow playfully arched,

children.text: karṇāsannaviśālacārunayanāḥ keśāntasaktasrajaḥ /
children.translated_text: with large beautiful eyes near their ears, with garlands fastened at the tips of their hair,

children.text: yad dāsyaṃ svayam aṅganāḥ sukṛtinām āyānti pīnoravas
children.translated_text: that women with full breasts come of their own accord to serve the meritorious —

children.text: tan māhātmyam uvāca saṃbhṛtaphalaṃ dānasya śauddhodaniḥ // SRKK_31 //
children.translated_text: this greatness, the fruit ripened [from past deeds], was spoken of by the Son of <s>Śuddhodana</s> [the <s>Buddha</s>] regarding generosity. // SRKK 31 //

children.text: paryasyatsahakārabhaṅgasurabhi preṅkhannimagnotpalaṃ
children.translated_text: Honey, tawny as <s>bandhūka</s> flowers, fragrant with the breaking of mango blossoms tossed about,

children.text: śrīmatkāñcanabhājane vinihutaṃ bandhūkatāmraṃ madhu /
children.translated_text: [with] submerged and swaying blue lotuses, poured into a beautiful golden vessel,

children.text: kāminyā śapathopanītam asakṛd yat pīyate kāminā
children.translated_text: which is drunk again and again by the lover, offered with an oath by his beloved —

children.text: hetuṃ tatra vadanti śuddhamatayo dānaṃ paraṃ śreyasaḥ // SRKK_32 //
children.translated_text: the wise of pure understanding declare generosity to be the cause of that [delight] and the supreme good. // SRKK 32 //

children.text: iti dānaguṇān niśamya saumya prayatātmā kuru dāna eva yatnam /
children.translated_text: Having heard these virtues of generosity, O gentle one, with a disciplined self, make effort in generosity alone.

children.text: tribhavogramahābhaye narāṇāṃ na hi dānāt param asti bandhur anyaḥ // SRKK_33 //
children.translated_text: In the great peril of the terrible [cycle of] the three worlds, there is no other friend for humans greater than generosity. // SRKK 33 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the Story of Generosity //

children.text: V. Puṇyakathā
children.translated_text: V. The Story of Merit (<s>Puṇya</s>)

children.text: yad dṛśyate jagati cārutaraṃ priyaṃ vā rūpaṃ kulaṃ priyajano vibhavāḥ sukhaṃ vā /
children.translated_text: Whatever is seen in the world as most beautiful or dear — form, family, loved ones, wealth, or happiness,

children.text: tat puṇyaśilpikṛtam eva vadanti santaḥ kalyāṇakāripuruṣasya na puṇyatulyam // SRKK_34 //
children.translated_text: the wise declare all that to be crafted by the artisan of <s>puṇya</s> (merit); nothing equals the merit of a person who performs good deeds. // SRKK_34 //

children.text: atyucchritonnatasitadhvajapaṅkticitrair nāgāśvapattirathasaṃkṣubhitair balaughaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With armies stirred by elephants, horses, infantry, and chariots, splendid with rows of lofty, raised white banners,

children.text: uddhūtacāmaravirājitagātraśobhāḥ puṇyādhikāḥ kṣitibhujo bhuvi saṃcaranti // SRKK_35 //
children.translated_text: kings adorned with waving <s>cāmaras</s> (fly-whisks) gracing their bodies, rich in <s>puṇya</s> (merit), traverse the earth. // SRKK_35 //

children.text: kauśeyakāśikadukūlavicitravastrā muktāvalīkanakaratnavibhūṣitāṅgāḥ /
children.translated_text: Clad in exquisite garments of silk, Kāśī-cloth, and fine fabric, their limbs adorned with strings of pearls, gold, and jewels —

children.text: yat ke cid eva puruṣāḥ śriyam udvahanti puṇyasya pūrvacaritasya kṛtajñatā sā // SRKK_36 //
children.translated_text: that certain men bear such <s>Śrī</s> (splendor) is the grateful reward of <s>puṇya</s> (merit) performed in former lives. // SRKK_36 //

children.text: āyuḥ sudīrghaṃ sukule ca janma kāntaṃ vapur vyādhibhayaṃ na cāsti /
children.translated_text: Long life, birth in a noble family, a beautiful body, freedom from the fear of disease,

children.text: dhanaṃ prabhūtaṃ parivārasaṃpad bhavanti puṇyasya mahāvipākāḥ // SRKK_37 //
children.translated_text: abundant wealth, and excellence of retinue — these are the great fruits of <s>puṇya</s> (merit). // SRKK_37 //

body.text: yac cakravartī pravarais tu ratnaiḥ sahasraputraiś ca samanvito 'pi

children.text: samudrasīmāṃ bubhuje dharitrīṃ tat puṇyaratnasya phalaṃ viśālam // SRKK_38 //
children.translated_text: ruled the earth bounded by the oceans — that is the vast fruit of the jewel of <s>puṇya</s> (merit). // SRKK_38 //

body.translated_text: That a <s>Cakravartī</s> (universal monarch), endowed with the finest jewels and a thousand sons,

children.text: vicitrapadmāsanamadhyasaṃsthitaḥ surāsurendrādinamaskṛtaḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: Seated in the midst of a splendid lotus-throne, always bowed to by lords of <s>Suras</s> (gods) and <s>Asuras</s> (demons),

children.text: yad brahmalokaṃ tv abhibhūya tejasā brahmā sadā bhāti tad eva puṇyataḥ // SRKK_39 //
children.translated_text: that <s>Brahmā</s> ever shines, surpassing <s>Brahmaloka</s> (the world of Brahmā) in radiance — that too is solely from <s>puṇya</s> (merit). // SRKK_39 //

children.text: yad devanāgāsurasiddhasaṃghair gandharvayakṣottamakinnaraiś ca /
children.translated_text: That the preceptor of the gods is forever worshipped by hosts of <s>Devas</s> (gods), <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Siddhas</s>,

children.text: saṃpūjyate devaguruḥ sadaiva tat puṇyaratnasya phalaṃ viśālam // SRKK_40 //
children.translated_text: <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and the best of <s>Kinnaras</s> — that is the vast fruit of the jewel of <s>puṇya</s> (merit). // SRKK_40 //

children.text: rūpaṃ vīryaṃ ca śilpaṃ ca vihāya vivaśā narāḥ /
children.translated_text: Leaving behind beauty, vigor, and skill, men go helplessly

children.text: paralokam ito yānti karmavāyubhir īritāḥ // SRKK_41 //
children.translated_text: from this world to the next, driven by the winds of <s>karma</s> (action). // SRKK_41 //

children.text: puṇyaṃ tv ekam ihātyantam anugāmi sukhodayam /
children.translated_text: <s>Puṇya</s> (merit) alone is the ultimate companion here, giving rise to happiness;

children.text: puṇyam anyair ahāryatvād dhanānāṃ pravaraṃ dhanam // SRKK_42 //
children.translated_text: since it cannot be taken by others, <s>puṇya</s> (merit) is the supreme wealth among all wealth. // SRKK_42 //

children.text: ye merum api vegena vikiranti diśo daśa /
children.translated_text: Even the winds of universal dissolution, which with their force scatter <s>Meru</s> (the cosmic mountain) in the ten directions,

children.text: te 'pi puṇyasya bhaṅgāya nālaṃ pralayavāyavaḥ // SRKK_43 //
children.translated_text: are unable to destroy <s>puṇya</s> (merit). // SRKK_43 //

children.text: puṇyaṃ na kledam āyāti catuḥsāgaravāriṇā // SRKK_44 //
children.translated_text: <s>puṇya</s> (merit) is not moistened or eroded. // SRKK_44 //

body.translated_text: By the waters of the four oceans, rising unrestrained in the deluge of universal destruction,

children.text: pradīptakiraṇāṅgāraiḥ saptabhir bhāskarānalaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Even when the earth is being burned by the blazing embers of seven suns,

children.text: kṣitau vā dahyamānāyāṃ puṇyam ekaṃ na dahyate // SRKK_45 //
children.translated_text: <s>puṇya</s> (merit) alone is not consumed. // SRKK_45 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the Story of Merit (<s>Puṇyakathā</s>). //

body.text:
VI. Bimbakathā
āḍhyo nirnaṣṭaśokaḥ kṣatasakalakalir locanānandapātraṃ

children.text: saubhāgyaśrīnidhānaṃ samupacitabalākrāntagātro yaśasvī/
children.translated_text: a treasury of beauty and <s>Śrī</s> (fortune), with accumulated strength pervading his limbs, glorious,

children.text: tejasvī kāntarūpaḥ pravacanacaturo dāntasarvendriyāśvo
children.translated_text: radiant, of lovely form, skilled in teaching, with all senses tamed like horses,

children.text: vyakto dhīmān pradātā bhavati bhagavato buddhabimbaṃ vidhāya // SRKK_46 //
children.translated_text: clearly wise and generous — such a one becomes by fashioning an image of the <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One) <s>Buddha</s>. // SRKK_46 //

body.translated_text:
VI. Story of Images (<s>Bimbakathā</s>)
Wealthy, free from sorrow, all conflicts destroyed, a vessel of delight to the eyes,

children.text: yāvantaḥ paramāṇavo bhagavataḥ stūpeṣu bimbeṣu vā
children.translated_text: As many atoms as there are in the <s>stūpas</s> or images of the <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One),

children.text: tatkartur divi bhūtale ca niyataṃ tāvanti rājyāny api /
children.translated_text: so many kingdoms does their maker surely obtain, in heaven and on earth;

children.text: rūpārūpyasamādhisaṃpad akhilaṃ bhuktvā ca sarvaṃ sukham
children.translated_text: having enjoyed all happiness and the wealth of <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) in the realms of form and formlessness,

children.text: ante janmajarāvipattirahitaṃ prāpnoti bauddhaṃ padam // SRKK_47 //
children.translated_text: in the end one attains the state of <s>Buddha</s> (<s>bauddhaṃ padam</s>), free from birth, old age, and calamity. // SRKK_47 //

children.text: dvātriṃśatā bhūṣitacārugātraḥ sallakṣaṇair lakṣitacakravartī /
children.translated_text: Adorned in beautiful limbs with the thirty-two marks, distinguished as a <s>Cakravartī</s> (universal monarch) by those auspicious signs,

children.text: bhavej jino 'nte jitadoṣaśatruḥ tāthāgatīṃ yaḥ pratimāṃ vidhatte // SRKK_48 //
children.translated_text: one who fashions an image of the <s>Tathāgata</s> becomes in the end a <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror), having vanquished the enemy of defilements. // SRKK_48 //

children.text: indriyāṇām avaikalyaṃ strītvadurgatidūratā /
children.translated_text: Completeness of the sense faculties, distance from womanhood and evil destinies,

children.text: janma mānuṣyakaṃ vaṃśa uccair ādeyavākyatā // SRKK_49 //
children.translated_text: birth as a human, high lineage, and having one's words heeded, // SRKK_49 //

children.text: jātiḥ śrutiḥ smṛtir dhairyam abhivāñchitasaṃpadaḥ /
children.translated_text: noble birth, learning, memory, steadfastness, attainment of desired prosperities,

children.text: sthāneṣv abhiniveśaś ca rāgādibhir abādhanā // SRKK_50 //
children.translated_text: establishment in the right stations, and freedom from affliction by <s>rāga</s> (passion) and other defilements, // SRKK_50 //

children.text: saṃbodhir iti jāyante viśeṣāḥ sādhusaṃmatāḥ /
children.translated_text: and <s>saṃbodhi</s> (perfect awakening) — these distinguished benefits, approved by the virtuous,

children.text: vidhāya buddhapratimāṃ stūpaṃ vā prāṇināṃ sadā // SRKK_51 //
children.translated_text: always arise for beings who fashion a <s>Buddha</s> image or a <s>stūpa</s>. // SRKK_51 //

children.text: na yāti dāsyaṃ na daridrabhāvaṃ na preṣyatāṃ nāpi ca hīnajanma /
children.translated_text: One who makes an image of the <s>Lokanātha</s> (Lord of the World) does not come to servitude, poverty,

children.text: na cāpi vaikalyam ihendriyāṇāṃ yo lokanāthapratimāṃ karoti // SRKK_52 //
children.translated_text: the state of a menial, lowly birth, nor impairment of the sense faculties in this world. // SRKK_52 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the Story of Images (<s>Bimbakathā</s>). //

children.text: nānāgandhaiḥ sugandhaiḥ snapayati sugataṃ puṣpadhūpāṅgarāgair
children.translated_text: One who bathes the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) with various fragrant substances, flowers, incense, and body ointments,

children.text: yo vā pūjāṃ karoti pramuditamanasā śravyavāditraśabdaiḥ /
children.translated_text: or performs worship with a joyful mind accompanied by pleasing musical sounds —

children.text: mandākinyāṃ vijṛmbhatkanakamayasarojasya kiñjalkareṇu-
children.translated_text: in the <s>Mandākinī</s> (celestial river), whose waters are pervaded by the pollen of blossoming golden lotuses,

children.text: vyāptāyāṃ snāti so 'nte sakalakalimalakṣālito yāti mokṣam // SRKK_53 //
children.translated_text: that person ultimately bathes, cleansed of all defilements and impurities, and attains <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). // SRKK_53 //

body.translated_text: VII. Story of Bathing (<s>Snānakathā</s>)

children.text: divyastrīpīnatuṅgastanajaghanaghanāghātavikṣobhitāyāṃ
children.translated_text: In the <s>Mandākinī</s>, disturbed by the impact of the full, high breasts and hips of divine women,

children.text: jṛmbhajjāmbūnadābjacyutasurabhirasodgāragandhaṃ kṣipatyām /
children.translated_text: emitting the fragrant essence flowing from golden lotuses blossoming there,

children.text: mandākinyāṃ suraughāḥ pratidinam udakakrīḍayā yad ramante
children.translated_text: the hosts of <s>Suras</s> (gods) daily delight in water-play —

children.text: nānāgandhodakena snapanaphalam idaṃ buddhabhaṭṭārakasya // SRKK_54 //
children.translated_text: this is the fruit of bathing the Lord <s>Buddha</s> (<s>Buddhabhaṭṭāraka</s>) with waters of various fragrances. // SRKK_54 //

children.text: mṛgamadacandanaṃ vidhusukuṅkumasevyarasaṃ
children.translated_text: Musk and sandalwood, moon-bright saffron, and delightful essences,

children.text: surabhimanoramāsitasitāruṇapītaruci /
children.translated_text: fragrant and lovely, of white, pale, ruddy, and yellow hue —

children.text: snapanam idaṃ ya eva vidadhāti muner manujaḥ
children.translated_text: the person who performs this bathing of the <s>Muni</s> (Sage)

children.text: sa bhavati vītamānasamalo jagur astamalāḥ // SRKK_55 //
children.translated_text: becomes free from the stain of pride and ego; their impurities are destroyed. // SRKK_55 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the Story of Bathing (<s>Snānakathā</s>). //

children.text: majjadvāravilāsinīkarakucaśroṇyūruvisphāritāṃ
children.translated_text: The <s>Mandākinī</s>, whose waters play upon the breasts, hips, and thighs of bathing women at its doors,

children.text: yat sphītasphuṭapaṅkajāṃ surapatir mandākinīṃ gāhate /
children.translated_text: abounding in full-blooming lotuses — that river <s>Indra</s> (lord of gods) enters,

children.text: kāntābhiḥ smaravihvalābhir asakṛl lokottamāyādarāt
children.translated_text: with his beloved ones, trembling with passion, repeatedly, out of devotion to the <s>Lokottama</s> (Supreme in the World) —

children.text: tad gandhodakapādyadhūpakusumasraggandhadānāt phalam // SRKK_56 //
children.translated_text: this is the fruit of offering fragrant water, foot-water, incense, flowers, garlands, and perfume. // SRKK_56 //

body.translated_text: VIII. Story of Saffron and Other Offerings (<s>Kuṅkumādikathā</s>)

children.text: yad rājā cakravartī viyati gataghanaiḥ kuṅkumāmbhaḥpravāhaiḥ
children.translated_text: That a <s>Cakravartī</s> (universal monarch) king, in the sky, in the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, flowing with streams of saffron-water,

children.text: karpūrāmodavadbhir malayajasurabhiśleṣaśītair yutāyām /
children.translated_text: fragrant with camphor, cool with the embrace of sandalwood,

children.text: gaṅgāyām aṅgasaukhyaṃ paramam anubhavan modate sundarībhis
children.translated_text: experiences supreme bodily bliss and rejoices with beautiful women —

children.text: tat tyāgāt kuṅkumāder guṇamaṇinidhaye buddhabhaṭṭārakāya // SRKK_57 //
children.translated_text: that is from the gift of saffron and other offerings to the Lord <s>Buddha</s> (<s>Buddhabhaṭṭāraka</s>), the treasury of virtuous jewels. // SRKK_57 //

children.text: mṛdaṅgavīṇāpaṭahapradānaiḥ kṛtvā tu pūjāṃ sugatottamānām /
children.translated_text: By offering <s>mṛdaṅga</s> (drums), <s>vīṇā</s> (lutes), and <s>paṭaha</s> (kettledrums), performing worship of the supreme <s>Sugatas</s> (Well-Gone Ones),

children.text: śṛṇoti śabdān suramānuṣāṇāṃ śrotraṃ ca divyaṃ labhate viśiṣṭam // SRKK_58 //
children.translated_text: one hears the sounds of gods and humans and obtains the distinguished divine ear. // SRKK_58 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the Story of Saffron and Other Offerings (<s>Kuṅkumādikathā</s>). //

children.text: gajaturagapadātisyandanaiḥ saptaratnair
children.translated_text: With elephants, horses, infantry, and chariots, with the seven jewels,

children.text: vrajati sutasahasrair vyomni yac cakravartī /
children.translated_text: with a thousand sons, a <s>Cakravartī</s> (universal monarch) travels through the sky,

children.text: śaśadharapariveṣacchattraruddārkapādas
children.translated_text: the sun's rays blocked by a parasol like the halo of the moon —

children.text: tad api phalam udāraṃ chattradānāt prasūtam // SRKK_59 //
children.translated_text: even that magnificent fruit is born from the gift of a parasol. // SRKK_59 //

body.translated_text: IX. Story of the Parasol (<s>Chattrakathā</s>)

children.text: vācālapracalālicakracaraṇavyālolapuṣpotkaraṃ
children.translated_text: A parasol with a mass of flowers swaying upon it, stirred by chattering, moving bees circling its edge,

children.text: nānāvarṇasugandhibhūrikusumanyāsena citrīkṛtam /
children.translated_text: made variegated by the arrangement of abundant flowers of various colors and fragrances,

children.text: chattraṃ cāruvicitrapattasahitaṃ caityāya yo yacchati
children.translated_text: whoever offers such a beautiful parasol with splendid leaves to a <s>caitya</s> (shrine)

children.text: prāpnoti kṣitipārcitaṃ sa hi caturdvīpeśvaratvaṃ dhruvam // SRKK_60 //
children.translated_text: surely attains sovereignty over the four continents, honored by the kings of the earth. // SRKK_60 //

children.text: hemacchattratiraskṛtārkakiraṇāḥ śrīmadvinītadvipa-
children.translated_text: With the sun's rays concealed by golden parasols, seated on the backs of majestic, well-trained elephants,

children.text: skandhasthā bahuratnabhūṣaṇavarāḥ śakrarddhivispardhinaḥ /
children.translated_text: adorned with abundant precious ornaments, rivaling the splendor of <s>Śakra</s> (Indra),

children.text: cāturdvīpakacakravartyavanipā yad yānti khe līlayā
children.translated_text: that kings of the four continents as <s>Cakravartīs</s> (universal monarchs) travel playfully through the sky —

children.text: tat tāthāgatadhātucaityakusumacchattrapradānāt phalam // SRKK_61 //
children.translated_text: that is the fruit of offering flowers and parasols to the <s>caityas</s> (shrines) of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> relics. // SRKK_61 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the Story of the Parasol (<s>Chattrakathā</s>). //

children.text: pade sugatasaṃpadāṃ sapadi satpratiṣṭho bhuvi
children.translated_text: One becomes firmly established on earth in the state of the <s>Sugata's</s> (Well-Gone One's) treasures,

children.text: prakāśitayaśā bhavaty akhilasattvadhātvāśrayaḥ /
children.translated_text: with fame proclaimed, a refuge for all sentient beings,

children.text: samunnatatarasthiraprakṛtisaṃpadā saṃśrito
children.translated_text: endowed with exalted, stable, and flourishing nature,

children.text: jinapratikṛtau janena yadi dhātur āropyate // SRKK_62 //
children.translated_text: if a relic is installed by a person in an image of the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror). // SRKK_62 //

body.translated_text: X. Story of Installing Relics (<s>Dhātvāropaṇakathā</s>)

children.text: śākrīṃ samantād adhigamya lakṣmīṃ dvīpāṃś ca bhuktvā caturo narendrāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having obtained the splendor of <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) on all sides and having enjoyed the four continents, kings

children.text: ante viśuddhaṃ padam āpnuvanti dhātoḥ samāropaṇato jinasya // SRKK_63 //
children.translated_text: in the end attain the pure state, by installing the relic of the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror). // SRKK_63 //

children.text: dṛśyante kāntimantaḥ śaśadharavadanāḥ subhruvo dīrghanetrā
children.translated_text: That mortals are seen in the mortal world as radiant, with moon-like faces, fine brows, and long eyes,

children.text: martyā yan martyaloke varakanakanibhāḥ kṣāntisauratyayuktāḥ /
children.translated_text: with complexions like fine gold, endowed with <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) and gentleness,

children.text: pṛthvīṃ yac cāpi rājā jalanidhivasanāṃ pālayaṃś cakravartī
children.translated_text: and that a king as <s>Cakravartī</s> (universal monarch) rules the earth girdled by the oceans —

children.text: tat sarvaṃ buddhabimbe bhavati tanubhṛtāṃ dhātum āropya bhaktyā // SRKK_64 //
children.translated_text: all that comes from devotedly installing a relic in a <s>Buddha</s> image. // SRKK_64 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the Story of Installing Relics (<s>Dhātvāropaṇakathā</s>). //

body.text:
XI. Maṇḍalakathā
bhavati kanakavarṇaḥ sarvarogair vimuktaḥ suramanujaviśiṣṭaś candravad dīptakāntiḥ / dhanakanakasamṛddho jāyate rājavaṃśe sugatavaragṛhe 'smin maṇḍalaṃ yaḥ karoti // SRKK_65 //
body.translated_text:
XI. Story of the <s>Maṇḍala</s> (<s>Maṇḍalakathā</s>)
One becomes golden-complexioned, freed from all diseases, distinguished among gods and humans, radiant as the moon; wealthy with gold, born in a royal lineage — such is the one who makes a <s>maṇḍala</s> in this excellent abode of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One). // SRKK_65 //

children.text: te prāpnuvanti sahasaiva janādhipatyaṃ dīrghāyuṣo vividharogabhayair vimuktāḥ /
children.translated_text: They quickly attain sovereignty over people, are long-lived, and freed from the fear of various diseases —

children.text: buddhasya ye hi bhuvanatrayapūjitasya kṛtvā bhavanti kusumaiḥ saha maṇḍalāni // SRKK_66 //
children.translated_text: those who make <s>maṇḍalas</s> with flowers for the <s>Buddha</s>, who is worshipped by the three worlds. // SRKK_66 //

children.text: dānaṃ gomayam ambunā ca sahitaṃ śīlaṃ ca saṃmārjanaṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Dāna</s> (generosity) is the cow-dung, combined with water; <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) is the sweeping;

children.text: kṣāntiḥ kṣudrapipīlikāpanayanaṃ vīryaṃ kriyotthāpanam /
children.translated_text: <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) is the removal of small insects; <s>vīrya</s> (vigor) is the effort of the act;

children.text: dhyānaṃ tatkṣaṇam ekacittakaraṇaṃ prajñā surekhojjvalā
children.translated_text: <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) is the one-pointed concentration at that moment; <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) is the radiant, well-drawn line —

children.text: etāḥ pāramitāḥ ṣaḍ eva labhate kṛtvā muner maṇḍalam // SRKK_67 //
children.translated_text: these six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) one obtains by making a <s>maṇḍala</s> for the <s>Muni</s> (Sage). // SRKK_67 //

children.text: divyaiḥ sukhaiḥ sakalabhogavaraiś ca yuktā martyā bhavanti kanakādhikacāruvarṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: Endowed with divine pleasures and all the finest enjoyments, mortals become of beautiful complexion surpassing gold,

children.text: padmānanāḥ svavikalāṅgaviśālanetrāḥ puṣpair gaṇasya vividhair vasudhāṃ vicitrya // SRKK_68 //
children.translated_text: With lotus-faces, large eyes with beautiful brows, and various limbs, they adorn the earth with diverse flowers for the assembly.

body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Maṇḍalakathā</s> (Story of the Maṇḍala).

children.text: kāntāpāṇisarojapattravidhṛtāṃ sadvarṇagandhojjvalāṃ
children.translated_text: The divine <s>sudhā</s> (ambrosia), held on lotus-petal plates in the hands of lovely women, radiant with excellent color and fragrance,

children.text: svāḍusparśasukhāṃ surāḥ surapure yad devavṛndārakaiḥ /
children.translated_text: delightful in sweet touch and comfort, which in the celestial city the <s>Devas</s> among the hosts of gods

children.text: bhāsvatkāñcanabhājaneṣu nihitām aśnanti divyāṃ sudhāṃ
children.translated_text: eat, placed in shining golden vessels —

children.text: tad buddhapramukhāryasaṃghaviṣaye nyastānnadānāt phalam // SRKK_69 //
children.translated_text: that is the fruit of offering food to the noble <s>Saṃgha</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.translated_text: XII. <s>Bhojanakathā</s> (Story of Food-Giving)

children.text: maitryā yaḥ saha kiṃkaraiḥ smararipuṃ nirjitya vajrāsane
children.translated_text: He who, with compassion and his attendants, conquered <s>Māra</s> (the enemy of love) upon the <s>Vajrāsana</s> (diamond seat),

children.text: kleśārīn api yo durantaviṣayān antaścarān durjanān /
children.translated_text: who also vanquished the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) — those endless, inner enemies difficult to overcome,

children.text: skandhārātim api prasahya sugato mṛtyuṃ ca nītvā vaśaṃ
children.translated_text: the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), having forcefully subdued the enemy of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) and brought <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death) under control,

children.text: prāptaḥ sarvarasāgrabhogavaśitāṃ so 'py annadānodayāt // SRKK_70 //
children.translated_text: attained mastery over the foremost enjoyment of all flavors — and even that arose from the merit of giving food.

children.text: saṃpūrṇasarvāṅgasamanvitaṃ ca śrīmatsukhādyapratibhānayuktam /
children.translated_text: Endowed with all complete limbs, possessing the radiance of glorious happiness and other qualities,

children.text: āyur balaṃ varṇam udārarūpaṃ prāpnoti vidvān aśanapradānāt // SRKK_71 //
children.translated_text: the wise one obtains longevity, strength, complexion, and magnificent form through the gift of food.

children.text: nirjitya śatrūn balavīryayuktān lakṣmīṃ samāsādya ca ye narendrāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having conquered powerful and valiant enemies and attained prosperity, those kings

children.text: svādūni bhojyāni samāpnuvanti bhojyapradānād dhi sadā tad etat // SRKK_72 //
children.translated_text: who enjoy delicious foods — that indeed is always the result of giving food.

body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Bhojanakathā</s> (Story of Food-Giving).

children.text: preṅkhannīlasarojagarbham amalaṃ yat padmarāgāruṇaṃ
children.translated_text: That which is pure, with the hue of a swaying blue lotus's interior, red as a ruby,

children.text: kāmyaṃ kāñcanabhājane vinihitaṃ prāleyamiśraṃ madhu /
children.translated_text: desirable honey placed in a golden vessel, mixed with snow,

children.text: kiṃcittāmravilocanapriyatamāpratyarpitaṃ pīyate
children.translated_text: offered by slightly copper-eyed beloved women and drunk

children.text: saṃgītadhvanisaṃgataṃ naravarais tat pānadānāt phalam // SRKK_73 //
children.translated_text: by excellent men accompanied by the sounds of music — that is the fruit of giving drink.

body.translated_text: XIII. <s>Pānakathā</s> (Story of Drink-Giving)

children.text: yad vaiḍūryendranīlapravaramaṇicitair bhājanaiḥ śātakaumbhair
children.translated_text: With vessels of gold studded with the finest <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl) and sapphires,

children.text: devā divyāṅganābhiḥ stanakalaśabharavyāptavakṣaḥsthalābhiḥ /
children.translated_text: the <s>Devas</s>, together with divine women whose broad chests are laden with pitcher-like breasts,

children.text: pānaṃ prītiprasaktāḥ saha madhu madhuraṃ mādhavaṃ vā pibanti
children.translated_text: drink sweet honey or <s>mādhava</s> (springtime mead), engrossed in delight —

children.text: proktaṃ prājñaiḥ phalaṃ tad guṇanicitagaṇe pānadānasya ramyam // SRKK_74 //
children.translated_text: the wise declare that to be the splendid fruit of giving drink, rich in accumulated virtues.

children.text: yat pānaṃ varṇagandhaprabhṛtiguṇayutaṃ kalpitaṃ tṛḍvināśi
children.translated_text: A drink endowed with qualities of color and fragrance, prepared to quench thirst,

children.text: śleśmāghātogravātapraśamanacaturaṃ pipphalīkhaṇḍacūrṇam /
children.translated_text: skillful in alleviating <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm), fierce <s>vāta</s> (wind), made with long pepper and sugar powder,

children.text: grīṣme prāleyabhinnaṃ śaśikarasadṛśe bhājane saṃskṛtaṃ tad
children.translated_text: mixed with ice in summer, prepared in a vessel bright as moonbeams —

children.text: dattvā saṃghāya bhaktyāmarabhavanagato divyam āpnoti pānam // SRKK_75 //
children.translated_text: having given such a drink to the <s>Saṃgha</s> with devotion, one goes to the abode of the immortals and obtains divine drink.

children.text: madhumadhuram udāram ādareṇa pravaragaṇāya dadāti pānakaṃ yaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who with respect gives sweet and excellent beverage to the foremost assembly,

children.text: divi bhuvi sakale sa pānam agryaṃ pibati ciraṃ pravarāṅganopanītam // SRKK_76 //
children.translated_text: drinks for a long time the finest drink, offered by excellent women, in heaven and on earth.

children.text: śraddhāprasannamanaso bhuvi ye manuṣyāḥ saṃghāya pānakavaraṃ pradiśanti kāle /
children.translated_text: Those people on earth whose minds are clear with faith and who offer the best of beverages to the <s>Saṃgha</s> at the proper time,

children.text: saṃsāraparvatadarītaṭavāsasaṃsthās te prāpnuvanti satataṃ madhuraṃ supānam // SRKK_77 //
children.translated_text: even while dwelling in the caves and slopes of the mountain of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), they constantly obtain sweet, excellent drink.

body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Pānakathā</s> (Story of Drink-Giving).

children.text: XIV. Vastrakathā
children.translated_text: XIV. <s>Vastrakathā</s> (Story of Cloth-Giving)

children.text: ye nīlapītaharitāruṇaśuklacitravarṇaprabhedaracitojjvalavastramālām /
children.translated_text: Those who offer garlands of splendid garments fashioned in varieties of blue, yellow, green, red, white, and multi-colored hues

children.text: yacchanti lokagurave sagaṇottamāya te prāpnuvanty abhimatapravarāmbarāṇi // SRKK_78 //
children.translated_text: to the supreme Teacher of the world together with his foremost assembly — they obtain the finest desired garments.

children.text: yaḥ saṃghāyāśeṣagaṇānāṃ pravarāya śrāddho bhaktyā cīvaramālāṃ pradadāti /
children.translated_text: He who, faithful and devoted, gives a garland of robes to the foremost of all assemblies, to the <s>Saṃgha</s>,

children.text: sa prāpnoti hrīvasanaṃ vastravariṣṭhaṃ kāṣāyaṃ ca kleśakaṣāyapratipakṣam // SRKK_79 //
children.translated_text: obtains the garment of modesty, the best of robes, and the <s>kāṣāya</s> (ochre robe) which is the antidote to the stain of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions).

children.text: dattvā satpiṅgacitrastabakaviracitā nīlapītāvadātai
children.translated_text: Having given beautiful garlands of robes — tawny, variegated, cluster-patterned, in blue, yellow, white,

children.text: raktair anyaiś ca ramyaiḥ suruciravasanaiś cīvaraiś cārumālāḥ /
children.translated_text: red, and other lovely, exquisite garments and <s>cīvaras</s> (monastic robes),

children.text: divyaṃ vāmuktavastraṃ sugatasutagaṇāyābhirūpo manojño
children.translated_text: or divine and liberating garments to the assembly of the <s>Sugata's</s> (Buddha's) sons — one becomes handsome and charming,

children.text: hrīvastrālaṃkṛtātmā bhavati paṭumatiḥ sarvadharmeśvaraḥ saḥ // SRKK_80 //
children.translated_text: adorned with the garment of modesty, sharp in intellect, and a lord of all <s>dharmas</s>.

body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Vastrakathā</s> (Story of Cloth-Giving).

children.text: XV. Puṣpādikathā
children.translated_text: XV. <s>Puṣpādikathā</s> (Story of Flowers and Other Offerings)

children.text: śakrādhikāḥ pravarabhogasamanvitās te padmendukāntivapuṣo varakīrtiyuktāḥ /
children.translated_text: Surpassing <s>Śakra</s> (Indra), endowed with the finest enjoyments, with bodies radiant as the lotus and the moon, possessed of excellent fame,

children.text: śatrūn vijitya rabhasā satataṃ bhavanti saṃghasya ye sukusumaiḥ prakiranti pūjām // SRKK_81 //
children.translated_text: they constantly conquer their enemies with vigor — those who scatter worship upon the <s>Saṃgha</s> with beautiful flowers.

children.text: nīlotpalapracayatulyaśarīragandhā vikhyātakīrtivimalāyatacārunetrāḥ /
children.translated_text: With bodily fragrance equal to a mass of blue lotuses, with renowned fame, pure, large, and beautiful eyes,

children.text: ratnopamā bhuvi caranti manuṣyabhūtā dattvā jine pravaradhūpam udāragandham // SRKK_82 //
children.translated_text: like jewels they walk upon the earth as humans, having offered excellent incense of noble fragrance to the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones).

children.text: vaiḍūryamuktāmaṇibhūṣitāṅgāḥ kauśeyavastrāvṛtasarvakāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: With bodies adorned with <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl), pearls, and gems, their entire forms wrapped in silk garments,

children.text: narottamāḥ sarvajanair upetā bhavanti buddhe surabhipradānāt // SRKK_83 //
children.translated_text: they become the best among men, attended by all people — through the gift of fragrant substances to the <s>Buddha</s>.

children.text: rogādibhiḥ prabaladuḥkhakarair vimuktāḥ snigdhānanāḥ kanakatulyamanojñavarṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: Freed from diseases and other powerful causes of suffering, with gentle faces, with complexions lovely as gold,

children.text: rājyaṃ hi ye vigatakaṇṭakam āpnuvanti bhaiṣajyadānavidhinā tad uśanti saṃghe // SRKK_84 //
children.translated_text: those who attain a kingdom free of thorns — that, the wise declare, is through the practice of giving medicine to the <s>Saṃgha</s>.

body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Puṣpādikathā</s> (Story of Flowers and Other Offerings).

children.text: XVI. Praṇāmakathā
children.translated_text: XVI. <s>Praṇāmakathā</s> (Story of Prostration)

children.text: yac cakravartī kṣitipapradhānaiḥ kṛtvāñjaliṃ kuṇḍalacārugaṇḍaiḥ /
children.translated_text: That a <s>Cakravartī</s> (universal monarch) is greatly worshipped with devotion, with folded hands and cheeks adorned by earrings, by the foremost kings,

children.text: bhaktyā svamūrdhnā bahu vandyate tad buddhapraṇāmāt kathayanti tajjñāḥ // SRKK_85 //
children.translated_text: bowing with their own heads — those who know declare that to be the fruit of prostration to the <s>Buddha</s>.

children.text: ye jātamātrāḥ prabhutāṃ prayānti śreṣṭhe kule janma sadaiva yeṣām /
children.translated_text: Those who from birth attain sovereignty, who are always born in the noblest families,

children.text: hastyaśvayānaiś ca paribhramanti kṛtvā tu te śreṣṭhatare praṇāmam // SRKK_86 //
children.translated_text: and who travel about on elephants, horses, and vehicles — they have performed the most excellent prostration.

children.text: prathayati yaśo dhatte śreyo vivardhayati dyutiṃ
children.translated_text: It spreads fame, bestows welfare, increases radiance,

children.text: harati duritaṃ sarvaṃ sarvaṃ hy arātim apāhate /
children.translated_text: removes all sin, and drives away every enemy;

children.text: sugatiniyatāṃ loke nṝṇāṃ karoti ca saṃtatiṃ
children.translated_text: it ensures for people in this world a lineage destined for happy rebirths,

children.text: phalati ca śivāyānte 'vaśyaṃ munīndranamaskriyā // SRKK_87 //
children.translated_text: and ultimately bears fruit in auspiciousness — such is the act of bowing to the lord of sages.

children.text: cakrī nṛpo yad balakīrtiyukto dvātriṃśatā lakṣaṇabhūṣitāṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: That a king becomes a <s>Cakravartī</s> (wheel-turning monarch), endowed with power and fame, his body adorned with the thirty-two marks,

children.text: saṃjāyate vai kṣitipapradhāno buddhapraṇāmād dhi phalaṃ tad uktam // SRKK_88 //
children.translated_text: foremost among rulers of the earth — that is said to be the fruit of prostration to the <s>Buddha</s>.

children.text: evaṃ bahuguṇaṃ matvā matvā kāyaṃ ca bhaṅguram /
children.translated_text: Having thus considered the many virtues of this and the perishable nature of the body,

children.text: buddhapraṇāmāt ko vidvān kāyakarmānyad ācaret // SRKK_89 //
children.translated_text: what wise person would perform any bodily action other than prostration to the <s>Buddha</s>?

children.text: kas taṃ na namaḥ kuryād dṛṣṭvā dūrāt punarbhavād bhītaḥ /
children.translated_text: Who, seeing from afar and fearing renewed existence, would not bow to Him,

children.text: kṛtvaikanamaskāraṃ bhavapāram avāpa yaddhetoḥ // SRKK_90 //
children.translated_text: by making a single prostration to whom one has reached the far shore of existence?

body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Praṇāmakathā</s> (Story of Prostration).

children.text: nānāsāraṅgarūpaprabhavamṛdumahadromasaṃślāghyavastrā
children.translated_text: Clad in praiseworthy garments of various colors, soft and great, made of the wool of diverse animals,

children.text: hemante garbhagehe priyatamavanitābāhuyugmopagūḍhāḥ /
children.translated_text: in winter, in inner chambers, embraced in the arms of their beloved women,

children.text: yat krīḍanti kṣitīśā vividharasavarair annapānaiḥ samṛddhās
children.translated_text: that kings sport, abundantly supplied with various delicious foods and drinks —

children.text: tat syād ujjvālikāyāḥ phalam atimadhuraṃ bhikṣusaṃghārpitāyāḥ // SRKK_91 //
children.translated_text: that is the exceedingly sweet fruit of an <s>ujjvālikā</s> (fire/bonfire) offered to the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks.

body.translated_text: XVII. <s>Ujjvālikādānakathā</s> (Story of Giving Fire/Warmth)

children.text: jvālātaraṅgavikasaddahanopagūḍhāṃ bhīmasvanāṃ śiśiraśītavināśakartrīm /
children.translated_text: Having given to the foremost among the best of sages an <s>ujjvālikā</s> — blazing with waves of flame, embraced by fire,

children.text: ujjvālikāṃ munivarapravarāya dattvā dīptaprabho bhavati devamanuṣyaloke // SRKK_92 //
children.translated_text: roaring with a fearsome sound, destroyer of cold and chill — one becomes radiant in the world of gods and humans.

children.text: gandharvāsurakinnaraiḥ sahacarā dedīpyamānānanā
children.translated_text: Accompanied by <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, and <s>Kinnaras</s>, with brilliantly shining faces,

children.text: vidyujjvālaśaracchaśāṅkasadṛśāḥ kāntābhir āliṅgitāḥ /
children.translated_text: resembling lightning-flames and the autumn moon, embraced by lovely women,

children.text: svarge yad vicaranti dīptavapuṣo līlāyamānāḥ surās
children.translated_text: that the <s>Devas</s> (gods), with radiant bodies, wander about in heaven, sporting playfully —

children.text: tad dattvāryagaṇāya śītasamaye cojjvālikāṃ śraddhayā // SRKK_93 //
children.translated_text: that is the fruit of giving an <s>ujjvālikā</s> (bonfire) with faith to the noble assembly in the cold season.

children.text: jitvā ripūn ye gajavājiyuktān pṛthvīṃ samantād anuśāsayanti /
children.translated_text: Those who, having conquered enemies equipped with elephants and horses, govern the earth on all sides,

children.text: dīptānanā hemavibhūṣitāṅgā ujjvālikāyāḥ phalam eva teṣām // SRKK_94 //
children.translated_text: with radiant faces and bodies adorned with gold — that is indeed the fruit of the <s>ujjvālikā</s> (fire-offering).

body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Ujjvālikādānakathā</s> (Story of Giving Fire/Warmth).

children.text: dharādharatiraskṛtaṃ paramadūradeśasthitaṃ
children.translated_text: An object hidden beyond the earth's horizon, situated in an extremely distant place,

children.text: susūkṣmam api vastu cātitimirotkarair āvṛtam /
children.translated_text: even exceedingly minute, and covered by masses of dense darkness —

children.text: karāgra iva saṃsthitaṃ yad aniruddhabhikṣur dṛśā
children.translated_text: that which the monk <s>Aniruddha</s> saw with his vision as if placed on his fingertip,

children.text: dadarśa sugatasya dīpaparibodhanāt tat phalam // SRKK_95 //
children.translated_text: that is the fruit of lighting a lamp for the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One).

body.translated_text: XVIII. <s>Pradīpakathā</s> (Story of Lamp-Giving)

children.text: buddhatvaṃ kila sugataḥ pradīpakena vyākārṣīn nanu nagarāvalambikāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Indeed, the <s>Sugata</s> (Buddha) prophesied Buddhahood by means of a lamp for the city-dwelling woman <s>Nagarāvalambikā</s>;

children.text: ko dadyād bhagavati na pradīpamālāṃ prāptyarthaṃ vimalamunīndralocanasya // SRKK_96 //
children.translated_text: who then would not offer a garland of lamps to the Blessed One, for the sake of attaining the eye of the pure lord of sages?

children.text: dūraṃ sūkṣmaṃ vyavahitaṃ dṛśyaṃ paśyanti ye janāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those people who see distant, minute, and obstructed visible objects —

children.text: jinapradīpamālāyās tat phalaṃ munayo jaguḥ // SRKK_97 //
children.translated_text: the sages have declared that to be the fruit of offering a garland of lamps to the <s>Jina</s> (Victorious One).

children.text: dṛśyante yat kṣitīśāḥ śaśadharavapuṣo dīrghanīlotpalākṣā
children.translated_text: That kings are seen with moon-like bodies and eyes long as blue lotuses,

children.text: devā yad devalokaṃ varakanakanibhā bhāsayanti svakāntyā /
children.translated_text: that <s>Devas</s> illuminate the celestial realm with their own radiance, resembling the finest gold,

children.text: rājā yac cakravartī maṇikiraṇaśatair bhāsayan gāṃ prayāti
children.translated_text: that a <s>Cakravartī</s> king traverses the earth, illuminating it with hundreds of gem-rays —

children.text: tat sarvaṃ dīpadānād bhavati tanubhṛtāṃ śākyasiṃhāya bhaktyā // SRKK_98 //
children.translated_text: all that arises from the gift of lamps to <s>Śākyasiṃha</s> (the Lion of the Śākyas) with devotion.

children.text: loke yad bhānti martyāḥ kuvalayanayanāḥ subhruvo hemavarṇāḥ
children.translated_text: That mortals shine in this world with blue-lotus eyes, beautiful brows, and golden complexion,

children.text: śakro yad devarājo daśaśatanayano bhāti divyāsanasthaḥ /
children.translated_text: that <s>Śakra</s> (Indra), the king of gods, the thousand-eyed one, shines seated on his divine throne,

children.text: yad brahmā vītakāmaḥ pravarasuranato bhāti divye vimāne
children.translated_text: that <s>Brahmā</s>, free from desire, honored by the foremost gods, shines in his divine aerial palace —

children.text: dattvā tad dīpamālāṃ prabhavati suphalaṃ śāstṛcaitye narāṇām // SRKK_99 //
children.translated_text: offering a garland of lamps produces that excellent fruit at the <s>Śāstṛ's</s> (Teacher's) shrine for people.

body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Pradīpakathā</s> (Story of Lamp-Giving).

children.text: XIX. Vihārakathā
children.translated_text: XIX. <s>Vihārakathā</s> (Story of Monastery-Building)

children.text: sarvarturamyavaraharmyatale narendrāḥ saṃgītigarbhajayajīvagirā ramante /
children.translated_text: On the terraces of excellent mansions delightful in all seasons, kings take pleasure in songs of victory and triumph;

children.text: śuddhāntavāravanitābhir aśītatāyāś cāturdiśāryayatisaṃghavihāradānāt // SRKK_100 //
children.translated_text: by the ladies of the royal inner quarters, from the gift of a monastery for the noble ascetic <s>Saṃgha</s> (community) of the four directions, against the cold. // SRKK_100 //

children.text: buddhapracodanavaco 'pi muner aśeṣam ārocya sāryayatisaṃghavihārahetoḥ /
children.translated_text: And having announced all the words of the sage prompted by the <s>Buddha</s>, for the sake of the monastery for the noble ascetic <s>Saṃgha</s>,

children.text: yaj jāgrato 'pi carataḥ svapataḥ sthitasya puṇyābhivṛddhir upariprabhavāpramāṇā // SRKK_101 //
children.translated_text: the increase of merit is immeasurable and ever-rising, whether one is awake, walking, sleeping, or standing. // SRKK_101 //

children.text: prajñāvajraprahārapravidalitakalikṣmādharasya prasādāt
children.translated_text: By the grace of him whose lip of darkness (<s>kali</s>-sin) is shattered by the diamond-blow of wisdom,

children.text: saṃghasyoddiśya sarvopakaraṇasubhagaṃ yo vihāraṃ karoti /
children.translated_text: he who builds a monastery, beautiful with all furnishings, dedicated to the <s>Saṃgha</s> (community),

children.text: prāsāde vaijayante pravaramaṇimaye stambhabhittau priyābhiḥ
children.translated_text: in the <s>Vaijayanta</s> palace, made of the finest jewels, with pillars and walls, together with his beloved ones,

children.text: sārdhaṃ sarvarturamye ciram abhiramate devaloke sa eva // SRKK_102 //
children.translated_text: he rejoices for a long time in the heavenly realm, delightful in all seasons, that very person. // SRKK_102 //

children.text: śrīmadvitānavarapaṅkajacitravastraṃ nīlādisaṃsthagitabhittigṛhaṃ pradhānam /
children.translated_text: Having given to the virtuous and excellent <s>Gaṇa</s> (community) a preeminent dwelling whose walls are covered with blue and other colors, adorned with splendid canopies and excellent lotus-patterned cloths,

children.text: dattvā gaṇāya guṇine pravarāya śākraṃ prāsādaratnam adhigacchati vaijayantam // SRKK_103 //
children.translated_text: one attains the jewel-palace <s>Vaijayanta</s> of <s>Śakra</s> (Indra). // SRKK_103 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the chapter on monasteries (<s>vihāra</s>). //

children.text: XX. Śayanāsanadānakathā
children.translated_text: XX. The Chapter on the Gift of Beds and Seats (<s>Śayanāsanadānakathā</s>)

children.text: paryaṅkaviṣṭarasamāstṛtatūlikāsu sīmantinīghanapayodharapīḍitāṅgāḥ /
children.translated_text: On couches, cushions, and mattresses spread with coverlets, kings whose bodies are pressed against the full breasts of women,

children.text: saṃśerate kṣitibhujo niśi yaiḥ pradattaṃ śayyāsanaṃ śamitadoṣagaṇottamāya // SRKK_104 //
children.translated_text: they recline at night — by those who have given beds and seats to the supreme one whose faults are pacified. // SRKK_104 //

children.text: divyastrīcārikāṇāṃ kalaravakalite citravastrāvṛtāyām
children.translated_text: On a bed made of jewels, great, fragrant with the scent of perfume, covered with colorful cloths, resounding with the melodious sounds of divine women attendants,

children.text: śayyāyāṃ ratnamayyāṃ surabhiparimalāmodavatyāṃ mahatyām /
children.translated_text: on that jeweled bed, vast and fragrant with the scent of fine perfumes,

children.text: kāntābāhūpadhānaś ciraṃ amarapure nirbhayas tatra śete
children.translated_text: with the arms of his beloved as a pillow, fearless, he sleeps for a long time in the city of the immortals —

children.text: yat tac chayyāsanānāṃ phalam idam uditaṃ bhikṣusaṃghāya dānāt // SRKK_105 //
children.translated_text: this is declared to be the fruit of giving beds and seats to the <s>Bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> (community of monks). // SRKK_105 //

children.text: karpūracandanavarāguruliptagātrā divyāṅganāstanayugāntaravartidehāḥ /
children.translated_text: Their bodies anointed with camphor, sandalwood, and the finest aloe, their forms resting between the breasts of divine women,

children.text: nityaṃ svapanti varavastrasutūlikāyāṃ stūpāya cātra śayanāsanadānatas tat // SRKK_106 //
children.translated_text: they always sleep on excellent cloth-covered mattresses — that is from giving beds and seats to a <s>stūpa</s>. // SRKK_106 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the chapter on the gift of beds and seats. //

children.text: yad dvīpāṃś caturo vijitya rabhasād yāto maghonaḥ puraṃ
children.translated_text: Having swiftly conquered the four continents and gone to the city of <s>Maghona</s> (Indra),

children.text: māndhātā tridaśādhipāc ca mudito lebhe yad ardhāsanam /
children.translated_text: <s>Māndhātā</s>, delighted, obtained half the seat from the lord of the gods;

children.text: saptāhaṃ ca hiraṇyavṛṣṭir atulāyātāsya yan mandire
children.translated_text: and for seven days an incomparable rain of gold fell upon his palace —

children.text: tat pātrapratipāditasya mahato dānasya citraṃ phalam // SRKK_107 //
children.translated_text: such is the wondrous fruit of great giving bestowed upon a worthy recipient (<s>pātra</s>). // SRKK_107 //

body.translated_text: XXI. The Chapter on the Field (<s>Kṣetrakathā</s>)

children.text: tac ca pātraṃ caturdhā tu gatiduḥkhādibhedataḥ /
children.translated_text: And that worthy recipient (<s>pātra</s>) is of four kinds, distinguished by the sufferings of the realms of rebirth and so forth;

children.text: pṛthak pṛthak phalaṃ tasmād viśiṣṭaṃ jāyate nṛṇām // SRKK_108 //
children.translated_text: from each respectively, distinguished fruit arises for people. // SRKK_108 //

children.text: vṛttānanāḥ kuvalayendusamānavarṇā martyāḥ sadā vimaladṛṣṭiviśālavakṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: With round faces, of complexion equal to the blue lotus and the moon, mortals always with pure vision and broad chests,

children.text: dānān manuṣyagatikeṣu samāpnuvanti ramyāṇi yānaśayanāsanabhojanāni // SRKK_109 //
children.translated_text: through giving to those in the human realm, they obtain delightful vehicles, beds, seats, and food. // SRKK_109 //

children.text: glāneṣu yan naravarāḥ pradiśanti dānaṃ dīneṣu durbaladhaneṣu kṛpānvitā ye /
children.translated_text: Those best of men who, filled with compassion, give gifts to the sick, the wretched, and those weak in wealth,

children.text: lakṣmīṃ hi te samadhigamya narendratulyāḥ krīḍanti nityamuditāḥ saha putrabhṛtyaiḥ // SRKK_110 //
children.translated_text: having attained prosperity, equal to kings, they sport forever joyful with their sons and servants. // SRKK_110 //

children.text: candrānanāḥ pravaradehaviśālanetrā bālārkatulyavapuṣaḥ śubhakīrtiyuktāḥ /
children.translated_text: Moon-faced, with excellent bodies and large eyes, with forms like the young sun, endowed with auspicious fame,

children.text: rājyaṃ narā vigataśatrubhayaṃ labhante sarvaṃ hi tat svagurumātṛjaneṣu dānāt // SRKK_111 //
children.translated_text: men obtain a kingdom free from the fear of enemies — all that is from giving to one's own teachers and parents. // SRKK_111 //

children.text: yad gacchanti kṣitīśā hayarathakaribhir vandyamānā janaughaiś
children.translated_text: That kings go forth with horses, chariots, and elephants, honored by crowds of people,

children.text: chattraiḥ sauvarṇadaṇḍaiḥ śaśikarasadṛśai ruddhatīkṣṇārkapādaḥ /
children.translated_text: with golden-handled parasols resembling moonbeams, blocking the fierce rays of the sun,

children.text: rājā yac chakravartī varanṛpatiśatair yāti sārdhaṃ pṛthivyāṃ
children.translated_text: that a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) king travels on the earth accompanied by hundreds of excellent kings —

children.text: kṣetre samyak tad etat pravaraguṇaphalaṃ śodhite dānabījāt // SRKK_112 //
children.translated_text: all this is the fruit of excellent qualities from the seed of giving in a purified field (<s>kṣetra</s>). // SRKK_112 //

children.text: māndhātā mudgadānāt kṣitipatir abhavat pāṃśudānād aśoko
children.translated_text: <s>Māndhātā</s> became a king from giving lentils; <s>Aśoka</s> from giving dust;

children.text: rājā vai kapphiṇākhyas tridaśapatir abhūt pañcasārapradānāt /
children.translated_text: the king named <s>Kapphiṇa</s> became lord of the gods from giving the five essentials;

children.text: citrākhyaḥ kṣīradānān madhu panasayutaṃ kṣīṇadoṣāya dattvā
children.translated_text: the one named <s>Citra</s>, from giving milk — having given milk mixed with honey and jackfruit to one whose faults were destroyed,

children.text: prāptaṃ vai kṣmāpatitvaṃ surapatibhavane siṃhanāmnādhipatyam // SRKK_113 //
children.translated_text: he attained kingship on earth and sovereignty named <s>Siṃha</s> (Lion) in the abode of the lord of the gods. // SRKK_113 //

children.text: dattaṃ bahv api naiva tad bahuphalaṃ satpātrahīnaṃ dhanaṃ
children.translated_text: Even much wealth given without a worthy recipient (<s>satpātra</s>) does not bear great fruit,

children.text: kṣiptaṃ balbajakaṇṭakākulatale kṣetre kṣite bījavat /
children.translated_text: like a seed cast upon ground overgrown with thorns and grass, in a ruined field;

children.text: rāgadveṣatamomalavyapagate pātre guṇālaṃkṛte
children.translated_text: but in a worthy recipient adorned with virtues, free from the impurities of passion, hatred, and darkness,

children.text: dānaṃ svalpam api prayāti bahutāṃ nyagrodhabījaṃ yathā // SRKK_114 //
children.translated_text: even a small gift grows to greatness, like a banyan seed. // SRKK_114 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the chapter on the field. //

children.text: XXII. Vicitrakathā
children.translated_text: XXII. The Chapter on Miscellaneous Matters (<s>Vicitrakathā</s>)

children.text: yo dharmaratnaṃ likhatīha nityaṃ śṛṇoti tac cintayate sadaiva /
children.translated_text: He who always writes the jewel of <s>Dharma</s> (the teaching), hears it, and ever contemplates it,

children.text: saṃbhāvanāṃ vā yadi cātra kuryāj jātismaratvaṃ labhate sa nityam // SRKK_115 //
children.translated_text: or if he should honor it, he always obtains <s>jātismaratva</s> (the ability to remember past lives). // SRKK_115 //

children.text: yad devaloke varakalpavṛkṣāḥ sarvārthasaṃsiddhikarā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: That in the heavenly realm the excellent wish-fulfilling trees (<s>kalpavṛkṣa</s>) fulfill all purposes,

children.text: devottamānāṃ sukhahetubhūtās tat gopradānasya phalaṃ viśālam // SRKK_116 //
children.translated_text: and become the cause of happiness for the best of gods — such is the vast fruit of giving a cow. // SRKK_116 //

children.text: yad garbhe paripuṣṭim eti śucibhiḥ pronnīyamāno rasair
children.translated_text: That one is nourished in the womb, being raised up by pure essences,

children.text: bālye yan madhusarpiṣī ca pibati kṣīraṃ ca kāle punaḥ /
children.translated_text: in childhood drinks honey, ghee, and milk at the proper time,

children.text: bhinnendīvarakesaradyutiyutaṃ pānaṃ ca yad yauvane
children.translated_text: in youth drinks a beverage endowed with the splendor of the petals of a split blue lotus,

children.text: vṛddhatve ca yathepsitaṃ vararasaṃ tad gopradānodbhavam // SRKK_117 //
children.translated_text: and in old age enjoys whatever excellent flavors one desires — all that arises from the gift of a cow. // SRKK_117 //

body.text: siṃhāsanaṃ pramudito ruciraṃ gaṇāya bhaktyā dadāti vidhivat khalu yaḥ sa dātā / siṃhāsanāni labhate pravarāṇy abhedyaṃ vajrāsanaṃ ca surapannagasiddhavandyam // SRKK_118 //
body.translated_text: He who, delighted, gives with devotion a beautiful lion-throne to the <s>Gaṇa</s> (community) in the proper manner — that giver obtains excellent lion-thrones and the indestructible <s>Vajrāsana</s> (diamond seat), worshipped by gods, <s>Nāgas</s> (serpent beings), and <s>Siddhas</s> (perfected ones). // SRKK_118 //

children.text: sauvarṇapātre satataṃ narendrā yat kṣīram aśnanti rasādiyuktam /
children.translated_text: That kings always eat milk mixed with essences in golden vessels,

children.text: lakṣmīsamṛddhāś ca narīr labhante padmānanās tan mahiṣīpradānāt // SRKK_119 //
children.translated_text: and that they, rich in <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity), obtain lotus-faced women — that is from the gift of a buffalo-cow. // SRKK_119 //

children.text: yānapradānena sadāturāṇāṃ sudurbalānāṃ vahanena caiva /
children.translated_text: Through the gift of a vehicle to those who are always afflicted, and through carrying the very weak,

children.text: saṃmānanāṃ vai kurute gurūṇām ṛddhiṃ samāpnoti naras tu tena // SRKK_120 //
children.translated_text: and by showing honor to teachers — a man attains supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>) thereby. // SRKK_120 //

children.text: aśvair vicitraiḥ satataṃ vahanti suvarṇapattracchuritair narendrāḥ /
children.translated_text: Kings are always conveyed by splendid horses adorned with golden trappings,

children.text: ṛddhyā ca gacchanti sudūradeśaṃ yānapradānāt tu tad eva martyāḥ // SRKK_121 //
children.translated_text: and they travel by supernatural power to far-distant lands — that is for mortals from the gift of a vehicle. // SRKK_121 //

children.text: hārārdhahāraiḥ kaṭakair upetāḥ krīḍanti deveṣu manojñavarṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: Adorned with necklaces, half-necklaces, and bracelets, they sport among the gods with enchanting complexions,

children.text: sārdhaṃ hi yat tat tridaśādhipena niḥsaṅgadānāt pravadanti santaḥ // SRKK_122 //
children.translated_text: together indeed with the lord of the gods — the virtuous declare that is from the gift given without attachment. // SRKK_122 //

children.text: bhītān samāśvāsayate sadaiva dhīmān naro vākpratipādanena /
children.translated_text: The wise man who always reassures those who are frightened through the offering of words,

children.text: sarvair na māraiḥ paribhūyate 'sau vākyaṃ ca nityaṃ madhuraṃ śṛṇoti // SRKK_123 //
children.translated_text: he is not overcome by any <s>Māras</s> (demons), and he always hears sweet speech. // SRKK_123 //

children.text: yad arhayantīha jinasya vākyaiḥ kleśāribhaṅgair bhuvi dharmadhātum /
children.translated_text: Those who honor the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (realm of truth) on earth with the words of <s>Jina</s> (the Victorious One), by vanquishing the affliction-enemies,

children.text: saṃsārasaukhyaṃ tv anubhūya sarvaṃ dharmeśvaratvaṃ pravaraṃ labhante // SRKK_124 //
children.translated_text: having experienced all the happiness of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), they attain the supreme lordship of <s>Dharma</s>. // SRKK_124 //

children.text: pratiśrayaṃ te pradiśanti santaḥ sarvatra kāle śramapīḍitānām /
children.translated_text: Those virtuous ones who give shelter at all times to those afflicted by weariness,

children.text: te yānti nākaṃ satataṃ prahṛṣṭāḥ śakreṇa sārdhaṃ ca sadā ramante // SRKK_125 //
children.translated_text: they go to heaven always rejoicing, and sport forever with <s>Śakra</s> (Indra). // SRKK_125 //

children.text: ye ropayantīha sukānanāni vṛkṣāṃś ca puṣpāṇi ca gandhavanti /
children.translated_text: Those who plant beautiful groves, trees, and fragrant flowers here,

children.text: cyutvāpi te yānti divaṃ manuṣyā udyānamālādyupabhogayuktāḥ // SRKK_126 //
children.translated_text: even after death, those mortals go to heaven, endowed with the enjoyment of gardens and garlands. // SRKK_126 //

children.text: kurvanti setuṃ viṣame pradeśe pānīyamadhye 'pi ca ye manuṣyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those men who build a bridge in a difficult place, and also in the midst of water,

children.text: svargaṃ sadā bhogasamanvitaṃ hi yānty uttamaṃ te varahemagātrāḥ // SRKK_127 //
children.translated_text: they always go to the supreme heaven endowed with enjoyments, with bodies of the finest gold. // SRKK_127 //

children.text: vāpītaḍāgāni suśobhanāni kṛtvā narāḥ svargam avāpnuvanti /
children.translated_text: Having made beautiful wells and ponds, men attain heaven,

children.text: ihaiva loke ca manuṣyabhūtā rājyāni ramyāṇi sukhāvahāni // SRKK_128 //
children.translated_text: and even here in this world, as humans, they obtain delightful kingdoms bringing happiness. // SRKK_128 //

children.text: kūpān maṭhān sattvasamāśrayāṃś ca vātātapatrāṇanimittabhūtān /
children.translated_text: Those excellent men who construct wells, rest-houses, shelters for beings,

children.text: ye kārayanti pravarān manuṣyās te devabhūtāḥ sukhino bhavanti // SRKK_129 //
children.translated_text: and structures providing protection from wind, heat, and rain — having become divine, they become happy. // SRKK_129 //

children.text: chattrāṇi ye vā pratipādayanti sūryāṃśutāpena suduḥkhiteṣu /
children.translated_text: Those who give parasols to those suffering greatly from the heat of the sun's rays,

children.text: chattropagās te jitaśatrusaṃghā bhavanti nityaṃ varasaukhyayuktāḥ // SRKK_130 //
children.translated_text: they become possessors of parasols, conquerors of hostile armies, and are always endowed with excellent happiness. // SRKK_130 //

children.text: pādāśrayaṃ citram upānahau ca sarveṣu sattveṣu diśanti bhaktyā /
children.translated_text: Those who devotedly give to all beings beautiful footwear and sandals as protection for the feet,

children.text: yānottamais te suciraṃ prayānti deveṣu martyesu sadopapannāḥ // SRKK_131 //
children.translated_text: they travel for a long time on the finest vehicles, always well-provided among gods and mortals. // SRKK_131 //

children.text: śaṃsanti ye jinavaraṃ guṇakīrtanena kāyapraṇāmakriyayā ca gurūṃś ca sarvān /
children.translated_text: Those who praise the best of <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones) by extolling his virtues, and honor all teachers by bodily obeisance,

children.text: saṃmānanāṃ gurukulāt samavāpnuvanti jātiṃ tathaiva vacanapratisaṃvidaṃ ca // SRKK_132 //
children.translated_text: they receive honor from the family of teachers, and likewise attain noble birth and the gift of eloquent speech. // SRKK_132 //

children.text: mṛdaṅgavīṇāpaṭahādibhir ye kurvanti pūjāṃ sugatottamānām /
children.translated_text: Those who worship the supreme <s>Sugatas</s> (Well-Gone Ones) with <s>mṛdaṅgas</s> (drums), <s>vīṇās</s> (lutes), <s>paṭahas</s> (kettledrums), and other instruments,

children.text: manuṣyabhūtāḥ sumanojñavākyāḥ śṛṇvanti śabdān sumanojñarūpān // SRKK_133 //
children.translated_text: as humans they become possessed of most pleasant speech, and hear sounds of most pleasing form. // SRKK_133 //

children.text: yaṣṭiṃ samāropayati prahṛṣṭaś chattraṃ ca ghaṇṭāṃ sugatasya caitye /
children.translated_text: He who joyfully raises a staff and a parasol and a bell upon a <s>caitya</s> (shrine) of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One),

children.text: chattrāvalīṃ vā kurute sa tena lakṣmīṃ samāpnoti naro viśālām // SRKK_134 //
children.translated_text: or makes a row of parasols — by that, a man attains vast <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity). // SRKK_134 //

children.text: manuṣyabhūto bhuvi yaḥ samantād īśatvam āpnoti balena yuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who, being a human on earth, attains sovereignty on all sides, endowed with strength,

children.text: keyūramuktābharaṇair upeto bhūmipradānāt tad uśanti santaḥ // SRKK_135 //
children.translated_text: adorned with armlets and pearl ornaments — the virtuous declare that is from the gift of land. // SRKK_135 //

children.text: bimbaṃ karoti pravaraṃ jinasya stūpaṃ ca vā chattravarair upetam /
children.translated_text: One who makes an excellent image of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor), or a <s>stūpa</s> furnished with the finest parasols,

children.text: dhātuṃ samāropayatīha yaś ca svargaṃ samāpnoti naras tu tena // SRKK_136 //
children.translated_text: and one who enshrines a relic here — by that merit a person attains heaven. (136)

children.text: ye buddham uddiśya mahānti nityaṃ kurvanti mṛdgomayalepanāni /
