children.translated_text: Those who, dedicating their efforts to the <s>Buddha</s>, constantly perform great anointings with clay and cow-dung,

children.text: puṣpaṃ phalaṃ bhojanapānakaṃ vā yacchanti te rājabalaṃ labhante // SRKK_137 //
children.translated_text: and offer flowers, fruits, food, or drink — they obtain the power of a king. (137)

children.text: dīpān udārān vividhāṃś ca gandhān puṣpāṇi dhūpaṃ guḍapānakaṃ vā /
children.translated_text: Those who give splendid lamps, various fragrances, flowers, incense, or jaggery-drinks,

children.text: diśanti saṃghasya tathā ca hema bhavanti te devasukhena yuktāḥ // SRKK_138 //
children.translated_text: and also gold to the <s>Saṃgha</s> — they become endowed with celestial happiness. (138)

children.text: stūpāṅganaṃ dhātuvaraṃ vihāraṃ ye śodhayantīha narāḥ prayatnaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Those people who diligently clean the <s>stūpa</s> courtyard, the relic shrine, or the monastery,

children.text: nirmālyam ebhyaś ca samudvahanti te hemavarṇāḥ sudṛśo bhavanti // SRKK_139 //
children.translated_text: and who remove the withered offerings from them — they become golden-complexioned and beautiful to behold. (139)

children.text: ujjvālikāṃ ye pradiśanti sadbhyaḥ śītāgame vastram athāpi geham /
children.translated_text: Those who give fire-brands to the virtuous, or clothing in the cold season, or a dwelling,

children.text: pānaṃ vicitraṃ varakanyakāṃ vā te janmabhūmau sukhino bhavanti // SRKK_140 //
children.translated_text: or various drinks, or an excellent maiden — they become happy in their land of birth. (140)

children.text: dīrghāyur eva bhuvi sarvarujā vimuktaḥ prāpnoti saukḥyam atulaṃ satataṃ prahṛṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: Long-lived indeed on earth, freed from all diseases, one attains incomparable happiness, ever rejoicing;

children.text: devodbhavāni vividhāni sukhāni bhuṅkte prāṇātipātavirataḥ khalu yas tu vidvān // SRKK_141 //
children.translated_text: one enjoys various celestial pleasures — this is the fruit for the wise one who abstains from taking life. (141)

children.text: dṛṣṭvā parasya vibhavaṃ na karoti cauryaṃ guptiṃ ca yaḥ prakurute parirakṣaṇārtham /
children.translated_text: One who, seeing another's wealth, does not commit theft, and who provides protection for the sake of safeguarding others —

children.text: prāpnoty asau draviṇasaṃpadam aprameyāṃ sarvais tu taskaranṛpādiśatair ahāryām // SRKK_142 //
children.translated_text: that person obtains immeasurable abundance of riches, which cannot be taken away by any hundreds of thieves, kings, and the like. (142)

children.text: dārān parasya parivarjayatīha yo 'sau dārān asau labhata eva manojñarūpān /
children.translated_text: One who avoids the wives of others in this world — that person indeed obtains wives of beautiful form;

children.text: śatrūdbhavo na hi janasya kadā cid eva lokasya vai bhavati viśvasanīya eva // SRKK_143 //
children.translated_text: enmity never arises from anyone toward such a person, and indeed one becomes trustworthy in the eyes of the world. (143)

children.text: nīlotpalasyaiva yathā hi gandho manojñarūpaḥ satataṃ pravāti /
children.translated_text: Just as the fragrance of a blue lotus, beautiful in form, always wafts pleasantly,

children.text: tadvan manuṣyasya hi vāti gandho mukhād asatyaṃ tu na vakti yaś ca // SRKK_144 //
children.translated_text: so too does the reputation of a person waft fragrantly from the mouth — one who does not speak untruth. (144)

children.text: sanmitrasamdhiṃ nṛpateś ca pūjāṃ bhaktyānvitaṃ putrakalatrabhṛtyam /
children.translated_text: Alliance with good friends, honor from the king, a family with servants united in devotion,

children.text: bhogān udārān sukham aprameyaṃ prāpnoti nityaṃ piśunād vimuktaḥ // SRKK_145 //
children.translated_text: abundant enjoyments, and immeasurable happiness — these one always obtains who is free from slander. (145)

children.text: ānandaśabdaṃ madhuraṃ śṛṇoti vākyāni nityaṃ sumanojñakāni /
children.translated_text: One hears joyful and sweet sounds, words that are always most pleasing;

children.text: deveṣu martyeṣu ca jāyate 'sau pāruṣyavākyād virato naro yaḥ // SRKK_146 //
children.translated_text: that person is born among gods and mortals — one who has abstained from harsh speech. (146)

children.text: dharmārthasatyaniratā khalu yasya vāṇī loke sadā priyatamā bhavatīha nityam /
children.translated_text: One whose speech is devoted to <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), truth, and meaning becomes ever most beloved in this world;

children.text: saṃpūjanāṃ sa labhate bahuratnajātair yāyāc cyuto vibudhalokam anantasaukhyam // SRKK_147 //
children.translated_text: that person receives worship with many kinds of jewels, and departing hence, reaches the world of the wise, of endless bliss. (147)

children.text: sa tīvrarāgo bhavatīha naiva bhogair udāraiḥ satataṃ ca yuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: One never becomes afflicted by intense passion here, and is always endowed with abundant enjoyments,

children.text: ādeyavākyaḥ pṛthukīrtiyuktaḥ parasvatṛṣṇāvirato hi yo vai // SRKK_148 //
children.translated_text: one whose words carry authority, who possesses great fame — one who has indeed ceased craving for others' possessions. (148)

children.text: prāsādikatvaṃ labhate sa nityaṃ sphītaṃ sukhaṃ rājyadhanādi loke /
children.translated_text: One attains serenity constantly, abundant happiness, sovereignty and wealth and the like in this world;

children.text: brahmatvam āsādayatīha samyaṅ maitrasya cittasya vaśān manuṣyaḥ // SRKK_149 //
children.translated_text: a person rightly attains the state of <s>Brahmā</s> through the power of a mind imbued with loving-kindness. (149)

children.text: svargāpavargaṃ samavāptukāmair narais tu nityaṃ samupārjanīyā /
children.translated_text: By people who desire to attain heaven and liberation, there should always be cultivated

children.text: astitvadṛṣṭiḥ paramā hi yasmāt sarvasya sā vai kuśalasya mūlam // SRKK_150 //
children.translated_text: the supreme view of right existence, since that is indeed the root of all that is wholesome. (150)

children.text: śraddhānirākṛtamater na virohatīha puṇyaṃ hy udārabhuvanatrayasaukhyakāri /
children.translated_text: For one whose mind has not rejected <s>śraddhā</s> (faith), merit does not fail to grow here — merit that produces happiness in the three magnificent worlds;

children.text: tasmān nareṇa viduṣā satataṃ niṣevyā śraddhā samastaguṇaratnanidhānabhūtā // SRKK_151 //
children.translated_text: therefore, by a wise person, <s>śraddhā</s> (faith) should always be cultivated, for it is the treasure-house of all excellent qualities. (151)

children.text: śraddhā śubhasya jananī jananī yathaiva saivādito manasi sādhujanair niveśyā /
children.translated_text: <s>Śraddhā</s> (faith) is the mother of virtue, just as a mother gives birth; she herself should first be established in the mind by the virtuous;

children.text: śraddhākarena rahito na hi bodhipakṣasaddharmaratnanikaragrahaṇe samarthaḥ // SRKK_152 //
children.translated_text: for one devoid of the vessel of <s>śraddhā</s> (faith) is not capable of grasping the multitude of jewels of the true <s>dharma</s> that constitutes the <s>bodhipakṣa</s> (factors of awakening). (152)

children.text: bhraṣṭo yathādhipatyād aiśvaryaphalāni na hy avāpnoti /
children.translated_text: Just as one who has fallen from sovereignty does not obtain the fruits of lordship,

children.text: śraddhendriyavibhraṣṭo na tathāryaphalāny avāpnoti // SRKK_153 //
children.translated_text: so one who has fallen from the faculty of <s>śraddhā</s> (faith) does not obtain the noble fruits. (153)

children.text: tasmān nareṇa viduṣā sugatādikeṣu kāryaṃ manaḥprasadanaṃ satataṃ hiteṣu /
children.translated_text: Therefore, by a wise person, the mind should always be made serene toward the <s>Sugata</s> (the Well-Gone One) and other benefactors;

children.text: niḥśeṣadoṣaśamanāya na cānyad asti śraddhā yathā dahati doṣagaṇaṃ samastam // SRKK_154 //
children.translated_text: for there is nothing else that pacifies all faults without remainder — as <s>śraddhā</s> (faith) burns away the entire host of faults. (154)

children.text: dīnāḥ kuvāsavo mūḍhāḥ kapālāṅkitapāṇayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Wretched, ill-clad, deluded, with begging-bowls in their hands —

children.text: darśayanty eva lokasya hy adātuḥ phalam īdṛśam // SRKK_155 //
children.translated_text: they show to the world such a fruit of one who has not given. (155)

children.text: dagdhasthūṇasamucchrayāḥ pratigṛhaṃ pretopamā bhaikṣukāḥ
children.translated_text: With uprights like burnt pillars, mendicants resembling ghosts in every house,

children.text: śaśvat kṣudvihatā bhramanti yad amī dehīti bāhūcchritāḥ /
children.translated_text: constantly stricken by hunger, they wander about crying 'Give!' with arms raised;

children.text: dūropadrutasārameyanivahā vyāvṛtya tiṣṭhanty api
children.translated_text: chased away by packs of dogs from afar, they stand turned back,

children.text: prāyo 'lpaṃ sakṛd apy amībhir aśanam dattaṃ na kasmai cana // SRKK_156 //
children.translated_text: and indeed not even a small morsel of food has ever been given by them to anyone. (156)

children.text: sūcīmukhāḥ kuharanetraviśuṣkagātrāḥ keśāmbarā ravikaraiḥ paripītabhāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: With mouths like needle-points, with hollow eyes and withered limbs, clothed in hair, their luster consumed by the rays of the sun —

children.text: pretāḥ sadā salilalālasayā yad ārtās tat pānadānavikalasya phalaṃ vadanti // SRKK_157 //
children.translated_text: that the <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts) are always tormented by the craving for water, this they declare to be the fruit of one deficient in giving drink. (157)

children.text: dānaṃ sarvasukhaṃ mahābhayaharaṃ bhāgyaṃ mahac cārthadaṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Dāna</s> (generosity) is the source of all happiness, the remover of great fear, great fortune and bestower of wealth,

children.text: nānākāraviśālakauśalapadaṃ sarvair guṇālaṃkṛtam /
children.translated_text: the foundation of extensive skill in manifold forms, adorned with all virtues;

children.text: tasmād dānam anekadoṣaśamanaṃ saṃsāraghorāpahaṃ
children.translated_text: therefore, <s>dāna</s> (generosity), which pacifies countless faults, removes the terrors of <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.text: kṣuttṛṣṇādisuśoṣaṇaṃ śubhakaraṃ kuryur narā yatnataḥ // SRKK_158 //
children.translated_text: dries up hunger, thirst, and the like, and produces auspiciousness — people should practice it diligently. (158)

body.translated_text: Thus ends the section on miscellaneous stories.

children.text: Saṃgrahaślokāḥ
children.translated_text: Summary verses:

children.text: puṇyotsāhanaṃ śravaṇaṃ durlabhaṃ tyāgapuṇyayoḥ /
children.translated_text: Exhortation to merit, the rarity of hearing, of renunciation, and of merit;

children.text: bimbaṃ snānaṃ tathā gandhaś chattraṃ dhātoś ca ropaṇam // 1 //
children.translated_text: the image, bathing, fragrance, parasol, and the enshrinement of relics; (1)

children.text: maṇḍalaṃ bhojanaṃ pānaṃ vastraṃ puṣpādivarṇanam /
children.translated_text: <s>Maṇḍala</s> (sacred circles), food, drink, clothing, description of flowers and the like;

children.text: praṇāmojjvālikādīpavihāraśayanāsanam // 2 //
children.translated_text: salutation, fire-brands, lamps, monastery, bedding and seats; (2)

children.text: kṣetraṃ vicitraṃ caivānta ity etā bahudhā bhṛśam /
children.translated_text: fields, and various topics — and at the end, these manifold

children.text: kathā dvāviṃśatiḥ proktā bhūyo dānasya varṇane // 3 //
children.translated_text: twenty-two stories have been told in further praise of <s>dāna</s> (generosity). (3)

children.text: XXIII. Śīlakathā
children.translated_text: XXIII. The Story on <s>Śīla</s> (Moral Conduct)

children.text: yathāmbupūrṇaḥ sabhujaṅgamo hradaḥ praphullaśākhaś ca sakaṇṭako drumaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a lake full of water but infested with serpents, and a tree with blossoming branches but covered with thorns —

children.text: śrutena vittena kulena cānvitas tathāvidhaḥ śīlaparāṅmukho janaḥ // SRKK_159 //
children.translated_text: such is a person who, though endowed with learning, wealth, and noble birth, is averse to <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct). (159)

children.text: varaṃ daridro 'pi suśīlavān bhaven na cārthavān apy analaṃkṛto guṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Better to be poor yet possessed of good <s>śīla</s> (conduct) than to be wealthy yet unadorned with virtues;

children.text: daridrabhāve 'pi hi sajjanaḥ stuto raso guṇānām amṛtād viśiṣyate // SRKK_160 //
children.translated_text: for even in poverty a good person is praised — the essence of virtues surpasses even <s>amṛta</s> (nectar). (160)

children.text: saṃmānayanti guravo guṇavantam āryaṃ tejasvino 'pi dhanino 'pi manasvino 'pi /
children.translated_text: Elders honor the virtuous noble one — whether powerful, wealthy, or wise;

children.text: tasmān naro narapater api yaḥ sakāśāt saṃmānam icchati sa rakṣatu śīlam eva // SRKK_161 //
children.translated_text: therefore, a person who desires honor even from the king, let that person guard <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) alone. (161)

children.text: loke sukhaṃ viṣayajaṃ sabhayaṃ savairaṃ dharmātmanaḥ kṛtamateḥ sukham uttamaṃ tu /
children.translated_text: Worldly happiness born of sense pleasures is fraught with fear and enmity, but the highest happiness belongs to one who is righteous and resolved in mind;

children.text: tasmān naraḥ sukham udāram ahāryam āryaṃ yaḥ prāptum icchati sa rakṣatu śīlam eva // SRKK_162 //
children.translated_text: therefore, one who wishes to attain noble happiness, exalted and unassailable, let that person guard <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) alone. (162)

children.text: yo bhraṣṭaśīlavinayasya vināśakāle trāsaḥ samāviśati śīlavato na so 'sti /
children.translated_text: The terror that seizes one who has fallen from <s>śīla</s> (conduct) and discipline at the time of destruction — that does not exist for the one possessed of <s>śīla</s>;

children.text: tasmāt prahṛṣṭavinayaḥ paralokam ante yo gantum icchati sa rakṣatu śīlam eva // SRKK_163 //
children.translated_text: therefore, one who wishes to go joyfully disciplined to the next world at the end, let that person guard <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) alone. (163)

children.text: śīlena niścayadṛḍhena divaṃ prayāti nātmaklamena na kudṛṣṭikṛtair vimārgaiḥ /
children.translated_text: By <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct), firm in resolve, one ascends to heaven — not by self-mortification, nor by wrong views and errant paths;

children.text: tasmād ṛte 'pi vanavāsam ṛte 'pi liṅgaṃ yaḥ svargam icchati sa rakṣatu śīlam eva // SRKK_164 //
children.translated_text: therefore, even without forest-dwelling, even without outward marks of asceticism, one who desires heaven, let that person guard <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) alone. (164)

children.text: śīlaṃ vināśaharaṇāvaraṇādirakṣā śīlaṃ dhanaṃ paramam āryam ahāryam anyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Śīla</s> (moral conduct) is the protection that removes destruction, obstruction, and the like; <s>śīla</s> is the supreme noble wealth that cannot be taken by others;

children.text: śīlaṃ sthiraṃ vyupaśame 'py anugāmi mitraṃ śīlaṃ vibhūṣaṇam ṛte 'pi vibhūṣaṇebhyaḥ // SRKK_165 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śīla</s> is the steadfast friend that accompanies one even in death; <s>śīla</s> is the ornament even without ornaments. (165)

children.text: na hy asti śīlasadṛśaṃ hitakāri mitraṃ snigdhāśayo na khalu śīlasamo 'sti bandhuḥ /
children.translated_text: There is indeed no friend as beneficent as <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct); no kinsman is equal to <s>śīla</s> whose disposition is affectionate;

children.text: mātā pitā ca tanayāya vidhātum icched yaḥ śīlam ūrjitaphalaṃ hitam ādadhātu // SRKK_166 //
children.translated_text: a mother and father who wish to provide for their child — let them bestow <s>śīla</s>, which bears abundant fruit and brings welfare. (166)

body.translated_text: Thus ends the story on <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct).

children.text: XXIV. Kṣāntikathā
children.translated_text: XXIV. The Story on <s>Kṣānti</s> (Patience)

children.text: sarvam etat sucaritaṃ dānaṃ sugatapūjanam /
children.translated_text: All this merit — <s>dāna</s> (generosity) and worship of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One),

children.text: kṛtaṃ kalpasahasrair yat pratighaḥ pratihanti tat // SRKK_167 //
children.translated_text: performed over thousands of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) — <s>pratigha</s> (hostility) destroys it all. (167)

children.text: na ca dveṣasamaṃ pāpaṃ na ca kṣāntisamaṃ tapaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no sin equal to hatred, and no austerity equal to <s>kṣānti</s> (patience);

children.text: tasmāt kṣāntiṃ prayatnena bhāvayed vividhair nayaiḥ // SRKK_168 //
children.translated_text: therefore one should cultivate <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) diligently by various means. (168)

children.text: manaḥ śamaṃ na gṛhṇāti na prītisukham aśnute /
children.translated_text: The mind does not attain peace, one does not enjoy the happiness of contentment,

children.text: na nidrāṃ na dhṛtiṃ yāti dveṣaśalye hṛdi sthite // SRKK_169 //
children.translated_text: one obtains neither sleep nor steadfastness when the thorn of hatred is lodged in the heart. (169)

children.text: na dviṣantaḥ kṣayaṃ yānti yāvajjīvam api ghnataḥ /
children.translated_text: Enemies do not perish even if one kills them for a lifetime;

children.text: krodham ekaṃ tu yo hanyāt tena sarvadviṣo hatāḥ // SRKK_170 //
children.translated_text: but if one slays anger alone, thereby all enemies are slain. (170)

children.text: vikalpendhanadīptena jantuḥ krodhahavirbhujā /
children.translated_text: A being, by the fire of anger fed with the fuel of false imaginings,

children.text: dahaty ātmānam evādau paraṃ dhakṣyati vā na vā // SRKK_171 //
children.translated_text: burns oneself first — whether it will burn the other or not. (171)

body.text: jarā rūpavatāṃ krodhaḥ tamaś cakṣuṣmatām api/

children.text: vadho dharmārthakāmānāṃ tasmāt krodhaṃ nivārayet // SRKK_172 //
children.translated_text: it is the slayer of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s> (wealth), and <s>kāma</s> (pleasure) — therefore one should ward off anger. (172)

body.translated_text: Old age is the destroyer of the beautiful, anger of the clear-sighted;

children.text: matkarmacoditā hy ete jātā mayy apakāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Impelled by my own <s>karma</s> (actions), these who harm me have arisen;

children.text: yena yāsyanti narakān mayaivaite hatā nanu // SRKK_173 //
children.translated_text: by which they will go to hells — they have indeed been slain by me! // SRKK_173 //

children.text: etān āśritya me pāpaṃ kṣīyate kṣamato bahu /
children.translated_text: By relying on them, my sin is greatly diminished through forbearance;

children.text: mām āśritya tu yānty ete narakān dīrghavedanān // SRKK_174 //
children.translated_text: but by relying on me, they go to hells of long suffering. // SRKK_174 //

children.text: aham evāpakāry eṣāṃ mamaite copakāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: I alone am the wrongdoer toward them, and they are my benefactors;

children.text: kasmād viparyayaṃ kṛtvā khalacetaḥ prakupyasi // SRKK_175 //
children.translated_text: why then, O wicked mind, having reversed [the truth], do you become angry? // SRKK_175 //

children.text: mukhyaṃ daṇḍādikaṃ hitvā prerake yadi kupyasi /
children.translated_text: Abandoning the principal [cause, such as] the stick and the like, if you are angry at the one who wields [it] —

children.text: dveṣeṇa preritaḥ so 'pi dveṣe dveṣo 'stu me varam // SRKK_176 //
children.translated_text: he too is impelled by hatred; let my hatred be directed at hatred itself — that is better. // SRKK_176 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the Story of Patience (<s>Kṣānti</s>). //

children.text: XXV. Vīryakathā
children.translated_text: XXV. Story of Energy (<s>Vīrya</s>)

children.text: vīryaṃ hi sarvaguṇaratnanidhānabhūtaṃ sarvāpadas tarati vīryamahāplavena /
children.translated_text: For energy is a treasury of all jewel-like virtues; by the great raft of energy, one crosses all misfortunes.

children.text: naivāsti taj jagati vastu vicintyamānaṃ nāvāpnuyād yad iha vīryarathādhirūḍhaḥ // SRKK_177 //
children.translated_text: There is no object in the world, when considered, that one mounted on the chariot of energy could not obtain here. // SRKK_177 //

children.text: yuddheṣu yat karituraṅgapadātimatsu nārācatomaraparaśvadhasaṃkuleṣu /
children.translated_text: In battles teeming with elephants, horses, and infantry, thick with iron arrows, javelins, and battle-axes —

children.text: hatvā ripūñ jayam anuttamam āpnuvanti visphūrjitaṃ tad iha vīryamahābhaṭasya // SRKK_178 //
children.translated_text: having slain the enemies, they attain unsurpassed victory: that is the thundering [power] of the great warrior of energy. // SRKK_178 //

children.text: ambhonidhīn makaravṛndavighaṭṭitāmbūttuṅgākulākulataraṅgavibhaṅgabhīmān /
children.translated_text: The oceans, with waters churned by hosts of <s>makaras</s> (sea-monsters), terrifying with the breaking of towering, agitated, surging waves —

children.text: vīryeṇa goṣpadam iva pravilaṅghya śūrāḥ kurvanty anarghaguṇaratnadhanārjanāni // SRKK_179 //
children.translated_text: the heroes, leaping over them by energy as though [crossing] a cow's hoof-print, acquire priceless treasures of virtue and wealth. // SRKK_179 //

children.text: rāgādīn uragān ivogravapuṣo viṣkambhavīryānvitāḥ
children.translated_text: Endowed with the power to subdue passions and the rest — [fierce] like serpents with terrible forms —

children.text: śīlaṃ sajjanacittanirmalataraṃ samyak samādāpayan /
children.translated_text: fully establishing good conduct, purer than the minds of the virtuous,

children.text: martyāḥ kāntatareṣu meruśikharopānteṣu vīryānvitā
children.translated_text: mortals endowed with energy, on the most beautiful summits of Mount <s>Meru</s>,

children.text: modante surasundarībhujalatāpāśopagūḍhāś ciram // SRKK_180 //
children.translated_text: rejoice long, embraced by the vine-like arms of celestial beauties. // SRKK_180 //

children.text: yad devā viyati vimānavāsino ye nirdvandvāḥ samanubhavanti saumanasyam /
children.translated_text: That happiness which the gods dwelling in celestial vehicles in the sky, free from dualities, experience —

children.text: atyantaṃ vipulaphalaprasūtihetor vīryasya sthiravihitasya sā vibhūtiḥ // SRKK_181 //
children.translated_text: that is the glory of energy firmly established, which is the cause of exceedingly abundant fruit. // SRKK_181 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the Story of Energy (<s>Vīrya</s>). //

children.text: XXVI. Dhyānakathā
children.translated_text: XXVI. Story of Meditation (<s>Dhyāna</s>)

children.text: kleśārivargaṃ tv abhibhūya dhīrāḥ saṃbodhilakṣmīpadam āpnuvanti /
children.translated_text: The steadfast ones, having overcome the host of enemies called afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>), attain the state of the glory of enlightenment (<s>saṃbodhi</s>);

children.text: bodhyaṅgadānaṃ pradiśanti sadbhyo dhyānaṃ hi tatra pravadanti hetum // SRKK_182 //
children.translated_text: they bestow the gift of the limbs of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>) upon the virtuous — meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) is declared to be the cause of that. // SRKK_182 //

children.text: janmaprabandhakaraṇaikanimittabhūtān rāgādidoṣanicayān pravidārya sarvān /
children.translated_text: Having torn asunder all the accumulated faults of passion and the rest — which are the sole cause of the continuum of births —

children.text: ākāśatulyamanasaḥ samaloṣṭahemā dhyānād bhavanti manujā guṇahetubhūtāḥ // SRKK_183 //
children.translated_text: through meditation, humans become the source of [all] virtues, with minds equal to space, regarding a clod of earth and gold as the same. // SRKK_183 //

children.text: jitvā kleśārivṛndaṃ śubhabalamathane sarvathālabdhalakṣyaṃ
children.translated_text: Having conquered the host of affliction-enemies, having attained in every way the target [that was] unattainable due to the destruction of auspicious power,

children.text: prāptāḥ saṃbodhilakṣmīṃ pravaraguṇamayīṃ durlabhām anyabhūtaiḥ /
children.translated_text: having reached the glory of enlightenment (<s>saṃbodhi</s>), consisting of the best qualities, difficult to obtain by other beings —

children.text: sattve jñānādhipatyaṃ vigataripubhayāḥ kurvate yan narendrā
children.translated_text: that which kings, free from fear of enemies, exercise as sovereignty over knowledge in [the domain of] <s>sattva</s> (goodness) —

children.text: dhyānaṃ tatraikahetuṃ sakalaguṇanidhiṃ prāhur āryā guṇaughāḥ // SRKK_184 //
children.translated_text: meditation, the sole cause of that, a treasury of all virtues — the noble ones, floods of virtue, declare [it to be so]. // SRKK_184 //

children.text: mohāndhakāraṃ pravidārya śaśvaj jñānāvabhāsaṃ kurute samantāt /
children.translated_text: Having constantly torn apart the darkness of delusion, the awakened Sun (<s>Saṃbuddha</s>) spreads the light of knowledge all around,

children.text: saṃbuddhasūryaḥ suramānuṣāṇāṃ hetuḥ sa tatra pravaraḥ samādhiḥ // SRKK_185 //
children.translated_text: for gods and humans — the supreme cause of that is <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration). // SRKK_185 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the Story of Meditation (<s>Dhyāna</s>). //

children.text: XXVII. Prajñākathā
children.translated_text: XXVII. Story of Wisdom (<s>Prajñā</s>)

children.text: prajñādhanena vikalaṃ tu narasya rūpam ālekhyarūpam iva sāravihīnam antaḥ /
children.translated_text: A person's form without the wealth of wisdom is like a painted figure — devoid of substance within;

children.text: buddhyānvitasya phalam iṣṭam udeti vīryād vīryaṃ tu buddhirahitaṃ svavadhāya śatruḥ // SRKK_186 //
children.translated_text: for one endowed with understanding, the desired fruit arises from energy; but energy without understanding is an enemy leading to one's own destruction. // SRKK_186 //

children.text: yo 'nekajanmāntaritaṃ svajanma bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyat kulanāmagotraiḥ /
children.translated_text: He who knows his own birth separated by many lifetimes — past and future — along with family, name, and lineage,

children.text: madhyāntavidyo 'pi janaḥ pravetti prajñābalaṃ tat kathayanti tajjñāḥ // SRKK_187 //
children.translated_text: one who knows the middle and the end — those who know declare that to be the power of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). // SRKK_187 //

children.text: yad buddho martyaloke malatimiragaṇaṃ dārayitvā mahāntaṃ
children.translated_text: When the <s>Buddha</s>, in the mortal world, having pierced the great mass of darkness of defilements,

children.text: jñānālokaṃ karoti praharati ca sadā doṣavṛndaṃ narāṇām /
children.translated_text: creates the light of knowledge and constantly destroys the multitude of faults in humans —

children.text: ādeṣṭā cendriyāṇāṃ paramanujamano vetti sarvaiḥ prakāraiḥ
children.translated_text: the commander of the senses, who knows the minds of other beings in every way —

children.text: prajñāṃ tatrāpi nityaṃ śubhavarajananīṃ hetum utkīrtayanti // SRKK_188 //
children.translated_text: wisdom, the eternal mother of all that is auspicious and excellent, is proclaimed as the cause of even that. // SRKK_188 //

children.text: kāryārṇave cāpi drdhaṃ nimagnāḥ saṃgrāmamadhye manujāḥ pradhānāḥ /
children.translated_text: Even when firmly submerged in the ocean of tasks, the foremost humans in the midst of battle

children.text: prajñāvaśāt te vijayaṃ labhante prajñā yataḥ sā śubhahetubhūtā // SRKK_189 //
children.translated_text: attain victory through the power of wisdom — because wisdom is the cause of all that is auspicious. // SRKK_189 //

children.text: tasmāt sarvaguṇārthasādhanakarī prajñaiva saṃvardhyatāṃ
children.translated_text: Therefore, let wisdom alone — which accomplishes all virtues and aims — be cultivated;

children.text: na prajñāvikalā vibhānti puruṣāḥ prātaḥ pradīpā iva /
children.translated_text: without wisdom, people do not shine — like lamps at dawn.

children.text: [matvaivaṃ svaparātmabhadracaraṇe saddharmasaṃsādhane
children.translated_text: [Having understood this, in the practice of good conduct for oneself and others, in the accomplishment of the true <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: jitvā kleśagaṇāñ chubhārthaniratāḥ krīḍantu dharmārthinaḥ //] 190 //
children.translated_text: having conquered the hosts of afflictions, let the seekers of <s>Dharma</s>, devoted to auspicious aims, rejoice!] // 190 //

body.translated_text: // Thus ends the Story of Wisdom (<s>Prajñā</s>). //

children.text: svargāpavargaguṇaratnanidhānabhūtā etāḥ ṣaḍ eva bhuvi pāramitā narāṇām /
children.translated_text: These six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) of humans on earth are the treasury of jewel-like virtues [leading to] heaven and liberation.

children.text: jñātvā naraḥ svahitasādhanatatparaḥ san kuryān na kaḥ satatam āsu dṛḍhaṃ prayatnam // SRKK_191 //
children.translated_text: Having known [them], what person, devoted to accomplishing his own welfare, would not constantly make firm effort in them? // SRKK_191 //

body.translated_text: // Thus the Narrative of the <s>Pāramitās</s> is completed in the <s>Subhāṣitaratnakaraṇḍaka</s>. //
The composition of Ācārya <s>Śūra</s>. //
